## Pull request 3 — wires, the colour law, the Inspector

**Wires are custom edges**, drawn with `getSmoothStepPath` and a midpoint chip through `EdgeLabelRenderer`. **The stroke says one thing and one thing only: what kind of push this is** (Kent, 2026-09-17). Five encodings, each readable without colour:

| What | How |
|---|---|
| Signal shape | Stroke pattern: `impulse` dot-dash · `step` solid · `ramp` a gradient along the stroke |
| Strength | Stroke width, from `|strength|`, regardless of sign. Four steps, not a continuous ramp |
| `sustain` versus `trigger` | A `sustain` wire is double-stroked. A `trigger` wire is single |
| `reflexive` | The wire loops back on itself and carries a **lag chip** reading the delay in days |
| Provenance | **An origin mark at the wire's tail**, where the arrow leaves its cause — not the stroke. Three steps: **●●●** `documented`, `historical`, `market_implied` · **●●** `argued`, `user` · **●** `asserted`, `simulated`. The exact word is in the Inspector |

**Why provenance left the stroke.** One channel cannot carry two meanings. The stroke already says `impulse` or `step` or `ramp`, and stack 02 gave it that job; asking it to also say `argued` or `documented` means a dot-dash-and-dashed wire that says neither clearly. A three-step mark at the tail says the useful thing at a glance — *is there a document behind this, or is it the model talking* — and the seven-way distinction, which nobody reads off a picture anyway, lives in the Inspector where there is room for the word. Build it as one small component, `OriginMark`, used by the wire and by the Inspector so the two can never disagree. INV-12 still holds: provenance is visible on every wire and no hue is involved.

**The midpoint chip** shows the conditional likelihood in the arrow-and-bar idiom the forecasting site Metaculus uses: the target's likelihood **with this arrow's source supposed true**. That number is **not computed here** and it is **not on the world** — stack 03a computes it lazily, one arrow at a time, through `POST /api/worlds/conditional`, because computing all of them costs a whole extra propagation per arrow. So the canvas asks for it when a wire is hovered or selected and caches the answer. Until it has one — and always, in this stack, since the route does not exist yet — the chip shows the arrow's push read back in words, *"+1.6 · a strong push toward"*, which is data already on the link and needs no arithmetic. **Never a guessed number.**

**The colour law**, in one place, as CSS custom properties added to `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` under a clearly marked new block. No existing token changes value.

| Axis | Channel | Tokens |
|---|---|---|
| Likelihood | Brightness — a five-step luminance ramp | `--p-0` … `--p-4`, each with its contrast ratio in a comment, as every existing token has |
| Direction of financial effect | Hue **plus a glyph plus a sign**, never hue alone | `--dir-up` (blue, ▲) and `--dir-down` (amber, ▼), both already in `tokens.css` |
| Tail risk | Texture | `--tail`, the hatch already in `tokens.css` |
| The kind of push | Stroke pattern, width and doubling | `impulse` dot-dash · `step` solid · `ramp` gradient; width from `|strength|`; `sustain` doubled |
| Provenance | **A mark, not a stroke** | The three-step origin mark at the wire's tail, above (Kent, 2026-09-17) |
| Branch identity | Its own small palette, on lanes and chips only — never on a tile's meaning | Violet, teal, rose, slate (*decided here*, accepted 2026-09-17). **Not amber**: amber already means "downward", and one hue cannot mean two things |

**The hover lens.** Hovering a tile dims everything not on its ancestor-or-descendant path to 15%. The research calls this the single highest-value interaction for legibility, and it is four lines of state.

**The Inspector is a persistent side panel and there are no pop-ups** (UX-10). It shows, for a claim: the full text, the resolution criteria and adjudicating source, the resolve-by date, the base rate with its reference class and its `k` of `n`, all three beliefs with owners, the evidence list, and — when the world carries one — the decomposition that makes the number explicable: *prior, then one line per incoming arrow with its push and its reason, then the result.* `spec/graph/belief.md` §B4 draws that block; copy its layout. **Reserve a slot directly under the range for "why is this band wide?"** — the answer is one sentence naming the claim whose own prior explains most of it (*"92% of this band is B's own starting number; pin that down and the band goes from 29 points to 8"*), it is computed from `World.range_shares`, and **it ships in stack 06, not here.** Leave the slot, leave a comment naming `range_shares`, render nothing. For an arrow: the rationale, the strength read back in words ("+1.6 — a strong push toward"), the mode in words, the lag, the shape, the sources with the day each was fetched, and the provenance in full — the word, with the same `OriginMark` the wire draws, so the mark and the word are one component and cannot drift apart.

**The path-product bar (INV-8).** Select a claim and a bar shows the multiplied-out likelihood of the path from the hypothesis to it, beside the story sentence. The product arrives on the world; this stack renders it. If it is absent, the bar says "no path shown" — it never multiplies anything itself.

## Pull request 4 — two worlds, the branch panel, the keyboard

**The ghost overlay.** Lay out the union of both worlds **once**, then draw the new world at full opacity and the old at 20% opacity, dashed, in the same coordinates. One layout, two paintings.

Each tile carries a diff state and that state drives its styling. In this stack there are four, all computed from the branch: `added` is solid with an accent ring; `killed` is ghosted, struck through, desaturated; **`downstream`** is drawn live — the claim your edit can reach, its number slot reading *"no engine yet"*; `untouched` is neutral, and it is the state the canvas can assert with confidence, because locality is a proven property and not a guess. The fifth state, `shifted` — `.61 → .18` with a directional chevron — arrives with the engine and needs no other change. **Never animate the diff as a crossfade** — `Space` toggles A ⇄ A′ as a hard switch, and the transition is scrubbable.

**The delta rail** sits beside the canvas. With the engine it is the terminal changes, ranked, one line each — *"the Polymarket Brent contract · .61 → .18 ▼ · largest on Oct 9"* — in the order the engine gave them, with **two columns that are never folded into the rank**: `range_width` (how unsure we are of the number) and **`agreement`** (the share of the 2 000 versions of the map that moved the same way — the vocabulary's reserved word for a number computed from how far independent runs differed, never self-reported). They answer different questions and a trader weighs them separately, which is why they are columns. Before the engine lands, **both columns render as an absence with its reason**, like every other number slot in this stack. **This stack does not rank and does not compute**: until the engine lands, the rail lists the terminals your edit can reach, in map order, each with an absence and a reason where the number will go. A rail that invented an ordering would be inventing the one thing the rail exists to tell you.

**UX-14, the overridden assertion.** A claim the user supposed true and that a later edit pushed back down never renders as plainly true. Its tile carries both states in order:

> **Supposed · Oct 1 → Retracted · Oct 2 · by "a confirmed military strike on Iranian territory"**

**While a claim is supposed, its tile shows the word where a likelihood would go** — *Supposed · Oct 1*, not `1.0` and not `.98`. The engine treats a supposition as a hard fact in every draw (stack 03a, Kent's decision of 2026-09-17), so there is no number to show, and inventing one would answer a question the user did not ask.

Its series then carries three named states after that, and the tile and the time axis both read them: **supposed** → **withdrawn** (the supposition has been undermined and no opposing push has arrived yet — labelled *"withdrawn — no live push yet"*) → **pushed**. On the Hormuz branch that is Oct 1 supposed, Oct 2 to Oct 4 withdrawn at `.35`, Oct 5 onward pushed to about `.07`. The three-day gap between the badge's date and the day the number moves is the honest shape of the answer, and the interface must be able to say so rather than smoothing it away.

Every part of that line is data on the world, not inference: the assignment gives *Supposed* and its date; the retraction gives the date, the arrow and the claim to name; `states` gives the three-state series. The **branch panel** lists that branch's edits in the order they were made, each with the badge its operation earns, so the surprising rule reads as a sequence rather than as a number that moved on its own.

**The six buttons and badges, word for word from `spec/vocabulary.md`'s Interface words table** — copy them, do not paraphrase, and never show a code name:

| Button | Badge afterwards |
|---|---|
| **Suppose this is true** (and **Suppose this is false**) | **Supposed · date** |
| **This happened** | **Happened · date** |
| **Add a claim** (hinted "…but this also happens") | **Added** |
| **Change this push** | **Retuned** |
| **Split this claim** | **Split** |
| **My own number** | none — the three-up belief chip is the badge |

and the derived one no button produces: **Retracted · date · by "…"**.

In this stack the buttons **build a branch and show it**; they do not move a number, because moving numbers is the engine's job. **My own number** and **Change this push** append an edit to the branch and the branch panel shows it immediately. **Split this claim** is visibly not yet live and says so (stack 06).

**The keyboard map (UX-9).** `⌘K` command palette · `j`/`k` between siblings · `h`/`l` along wires between layers — arrow movement follows the *wires*, not screen space · `E` intervene · `B` branch · `Space` A ⇄ A′ · `?` the shortcuts sheet. Focus is always visible, using `--focus`. Everything reachable by keyboard alone, end to end.

**Reduced motion (UX-7).** The motion budget is three animations and no more: the propagation wave (wires draw in causal order, about 200 milliseconds, staggered 60 milliseconds down the map), branch creation, and the belief number-roll. Everything else is at most 120 milliseconds of opacity. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the **ordering survives and the tweening goes** — per-layer instant reveals, a number swap instead of a roll, a hard cut instead of a ghost transition. Never remove the ordering: the ordering is the causality.

**The outline view (UX-12).** The map also exists as a nested list with `role="tree"`, each item read as a sentence — *"Brent crude settles below $68 for five sessions, 61 per cent likely, caused by the war-risk premium falling"*. A re-propagation announces itself through `aria-live="polite"`: *"Branch created. Six claims changed, one retracted."*

**Tests** (decision record 0008, layer 4):

- `frontend/src/graph/__tests__/layout.test.ts` — pinned tiles keep their positions across an incremental layout; the union layout used for a diff is stable.
- `frontend/src/graph/__tests__/diffState.test.ts` — the reducer maps a base map plus a branch to the four structural states, and the claim the strike branch provably cannot reach comes out `untouched`.
- `frontend/src/world/__tests__/branchReducer.test.ts` — the intervention panel appends edits in order and never edits one in place.
- `frontend/src/components/__tests__/beliefChip.test.tsx` — **`test_chip_never_shows_more_than_two_significant_figures`**, that the range is never omitted, that an absent number renders its reason, and that a supposed claim renders the word rather than a likelihood. This is decision record 0005's promised frontend rendering test; it is the one test that holds NFR-1 up.
- One end-to-end browser test with Playwright: open the Hormuz map, the tiles draw, open the strike branch, downstream tiles change and the fully separated claim does not, and H's tile reads *Supposed · Oct 1 → Retracted · Oct 2 · by "…"*.
- A fifth continuous-integration job, `e2e`, running that one test. **No API key in it** (INV-13).

Kent vetoes a template-looking interface on sight, so the coordinator looks for the template first.

1. Does anything look like a component library's defaults — a rounded blue button, a drop shadow, a system font stack, a default focus ring?
2. Is there a spinner anywhere? A pop-up? A dialog you have to dismiss? Any of the three is a veto.
3. **Convert the screenshot to greyscale.** Does every arrow still say what kind it is and where it came from, every direction still read up or down, every tail still show as texture? If not, INV-12 is broken.
4. Is any number on screen showing more than two significant figures, or missing its range?
5. Is there a number whose origin cannot be named in one click? Is there a number nobody computed — an empty slot filled in rather than left as an absence with a reason?
6. Is the map layered left to right, or is it a hairball with crossings?
7. Is any text below 11 pixels? Is any text under 4.5 to 1 contrast, in either theme?
8. Is the tile 280 pixels wide and on the 8-pixel grid? Measure it, do not eyeball it.
9. Tab through the whole screen with the keyboard only: is focus always visible, and does arrow movement follow the wires?
10. Turn on reduced motion: is the ordering still there and the tweening gone?
11. Are the six buttons and badges word for word the Interface words table?
12. Does a claim that was supposed and then overridden say so on its tile?

### The gate

**M3b** — stack 03b complete: four pull requests open and green; the Hormuz map draws, wires carry their five encodings, the Inspector answers "why", two worlds lay over each other, UX-14 renders, the keyboard works end to end, the `e2e` job is green. Kent has looked at it and nothing triggered a veto.

**M3** is both gates: the engine computes it and the canvas shows it. Stack 04 joins them by switching `WorldSource` to `ApiWorldSource`, which fills the empty number slots and adds the fifth diff state. Nothing is deleted at that point, because nothing false was written.

1	# The range under a computed likelihood — research summary (Opus agent, 2026-09-17)
2	
3	Condensed by the coordinator from the agent's report. Feeds decision record 0014 and `spec/multiverse/propagation.md`.
4	
5	## The idea
6	Two kinds of not-knowing, kept apart. **How the dice fall** (aleatory) is already inside `p`. **How sure we are of the numbers we put in** (epistemic) is the range. A wide range means "we are not sure what number to give you; more homework would move it" — never "the event is more volatile". Standard name: second-order / two-dimensional Monte Carlo (Cullen & Frey 1999; Vose 2000; EPA 1997 Guiding Principles for Monte Carlo Analysis; Der Kiureghian & Ditlevsen 2009).
7	
8	## What a stated {p, lo, hi} defines
9	**Split logit-normal**: median `p`; `lo`, `hi` = 10th / 90th percentiles; the two halves fitted separately on the log-odds scale (`s_lo = (logit p − logit lo)/1.2816`, `s_hi = (logit hi − logit p)/1.2816`). Honours all three numbers exactly, even skewed ranges; stays in (0,1) without clamping. Evidence: the fixture's hand-written ranges are near-symmetric on log-odds (mean gap ratio 0.94) and skewed on probability (1.26). Beta cannot honour three numbers. "8 times in 10" is the phrase. Consequence: mean sits slightly above median when p < .5 (H: .35 → .36), so `prior.p` and `beliefs.model.p` differ by a hair for the hypothesis.
10	
11	## Designs measured on Hormuz claim B at day 45 (exact truth by enumeration: .35 (.20–.49))
12	| Design | Reports | Seed wobble of band edges |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| A three runs (all lo / all hi) | .19–.50 — not a bound: R→B is negative, true box corner is .158–.567 | none |
15	| B 20 batches × 500 | .25–.46 — 26% of width is binomial noise; 28% too narrow | ±.021 |
16	| C delta method (analytic) | .22–.52 — accurate to .004 but 50× slower (one propagation per parameter); first-order only | none |
17	| **D nested, K=2000 outer (numpy Latin hypercube) × m=8 inner, Rao-Blackwellised, noise-corrected** | **.20–.50** | **±.002/±.003**, ~10 ms at 60 propositions |
18	
19	Noise correction (law of total variance): `f = sqrt(max(0, 1 − mean(inner_var/m)/var(q)))`; `q_corrected = mean + (q − mean)·f`. Needs m ≥ 2. numpy-only LHS is three lines; scipy not worth a dependency. Two seed streams from the one seed: `params` (K×d hypercube; **must not depend on the branch**, so base and branch share the same versions) and `worlds`.
20	
21	## What it gives the rest of the product
22	- **FR-21 for free**: first-order variance shares from the same outer sample (bin estimator, six numpy lines). Hormuz B: 92% of the band is B's own prior; pin it down → band 29 points → 8. Everything else < half a point. Better than "sensitivity × width".
23	- **Diff**: read the shift off the **paired** difference (same parameter draws), never band overlap. Hormuz do(H): bands overlap by a third, yet 100% of versions move the same way (+.10, 10–90 +.07 to +.13). Proposed: `shifted` = moved ≥ .005 AND same direction in ≥ 90% of versions; report that share as **agreement** (vocabulary's reserved word).
24	- **do** collapses the target's own band but does NOT reliably narrow downstream (B's width .292 → .323 under do(H): the logistic is steeper at .45). Show instead: H's share of B's band 2.6% → 0%.
25	- **observe**: reject in the inner loop, then reweight outer draws by survival share (importance weighting, five lines). Warn when survival is low.
26	- **FR-24** payoff distribution reads the pooled K×m worlds (both kinds of not-knowing together) and says so.
27	- A terminal's band is dominated by **its own prior's band** (factor p(1−p) ≤ ¼ × effect size on upstream ranges). Do not build the demo around "widen H, watch B widen" — it moves 4%.
28	
29	## Link strengths
30	No `strength_lo/hi`. Derive spread from `provenance` (documented/historical/market_implied 0.15 · argued/user 0.40 · simulated 0.50 · asserted 0.60) — "how well-backed" becomes "how wide" with no extra elicitation. Widening on Hormuz: +8%. Ship in **stack 04** (in 03a every fixture arrow is hand-written argued/asserted, so it would be uniform). 03a: strengths fixed, stated as such.
31	
32	## Literature on trusting LLM-stated ranges
33	Systematically too narrow (FermiEval 2025: nominal 90% → 28% coverage; QuantSightBench 2026); not coherent under rewording (Paleka et al. ICLR 2025); measured disagreement beats self-report (Farquhar et al. Nature 2024); every state-of-the-art forecaster ensembles (Halawi 2024; AIA Forecaster 2025). So in stack 04 (FR-8, N≈8 runs): point = trimmed mean; `σ_prior = max(stated, across-run spread)` — a measured number ("agreement"), with the stated range as a floor. Nothing is calibrated; say so on the chip.
34	
35	## Rejected formalisms (for the record)
36	Credal networks (NP-hard beyond binary polytrees), p-boxes (not rigour-preserving with repeated variables — shared ancestors), Dempster–Shafer (#P-complete), subjective logic (beautiful "wider = less sure" presentation, unsound deduction with shared ancestors), pure MacKay-κ moment propagation (parents are binary, not Gaussian).
37	
38	## Flag
39	With "tile reads at its own resolve-by day", the fixture's impulses have mostly faded by then (H→B at 0.37 of full size on day 45; B→M1 at 0.24 on day 30), so computed numbers land near the priors (M1 ≈ .42 vs the fixture's illustrative .61). The golden test asserts directions, not values, so it is safe — but the fixture's illustrative `beliefs.model` values and/or its half-lives and resolve-by windows deserve a look in 03a pull request 3.
40	
41	## Proposed wording
42	Chip label: **model interval, uncalibrated** · how sure we are of `.35` — not how much the world can move. Hover: "Across 2 000 versions of this map — each one a set of numbers this model would have stood behind — the answer landed between .20 and .49 eight times in ten. Nobody has checked whether that 8-in-10 holds up; no claim on this map has resolved yet." Record title: *ADR-0014: A supposition ends when something pushes back; a range says how sure we are of the number, not how the dice fall.*
43

1	# Kent's decisions on stack 03's open design questions — 2026-09-17, second round
2	
3	Asked through the question tool after an Opus design review of every open question in pull requests #18, #19, #21 and the canvas branch. Kent took the recommended option on all eleven and approved the fourteen small ones as a block. **All of these are settled. Reopen nothing.** Each is marked below with where it lands.
4	
5	## The eleven
6	
7	| # | Topic | Decision (Kent, 2026-09-17) | Lands in |
8	|---|---|---|---|
9	| K1 | **Feedback arrows** | **One named rule, written once in `spec/multiverse/interventions.md`:** *the map the engine works through is the map with feedback (reflexive) arrows set aside. Anything that asks "what can move" reads that map — the affected set, diff states, propagation's ordering, layering. Anything that asks "what can I walk to" reads the whole map — the hover lens, `h`/`l`, the outline.* Every other chapter cites it instead of re-deciding. A named test, `test_a_feedback_arrow_never_carries_a_change`, fails loudly the day stack 06 unrolls them and points at the one sentence to change. R is `untouched` on the strike branch | `interventions.md`; cited by `propagation.md`, `diff.md`, `diff-view.md`, `layout-and-zoom.md`, `keyboard-and-access.md`, `tiles-ports-wires.md`; `domain/patch.py` `affected_set`; tests |
10	| K2 | **Rounding** | **Two significant figures on the number AND both range ends, plus a certainty guard: a chip never prints `1.0` or `.0` — it prints `>.99` and `<.01`.** `.06` prints `.060`. NFR-1's example becomes `.35 (.22–.50)`; `belief.md` §B3's example likewise, and its open question 5 closes | PRD NFR-1; `belief.md`; `keyboard-and-access.md` B6; `BeliefChip.tsx` + test |
11	| K3 | **The chip's hover sentence** | **Two sentences, picked by whether a world computed anything.** `WorldView` gains one optional field, `versions`. Present → record 0014's label and sentence, word for word. Absent → the *stated* sentence the Inspector already uses under PRIOR: "this range is stated, not computed — it says how sure the elicitation was." No new copy; chip and Inspector share the two sentences so they cannot drift | `tiles-ports-wires.md`, `inspector.md`, `diff-view.md` (`WorldView`); `world/types.ts`, `BeliefChip.tsx` + test |
12	| K4 | **`killed`** | **Forced false, full stop.** "No path left from the hypothesis" stops being a diff state; it is a fact about the *path*, reported by the Inspector's path bar: "no path from the hypothesis reaches this claim any more." | `diff.md`, `vocabulary.md`, `diff-view.md`, `inspector.md`; `domain/diff.py`; the canvas's structural `killed` |
13	| K5 | **The rank's path; "how firm"** | **Path = the best-backed route** — over every path from *any* differing edit's subject to the terminal, the one whose weakest arrow is strongest (widest bottleneck; a ten-line Dijkstra variant), read over **the same graph the affected set is computed over**. "Shortest" and "which subject" both disappear. **`range_width` = the width of world B's own band on that claim at `at_day`** — the same quantity the tile shows. On Hormuz nothing changes: M1 0.6, N1 0.3 | `diff.md`; `domain/diff.py`; `diff-view.md`; the path bar uses the same path |
14	| K6 | **A fourth refusal code** | **`edit_not_applicable`** — "this edit cannot be folded onto this map as written". Covers `refine` (not built), an `insert` whose arrow touches neither end of the new claim, and a branch chain that loops or names a missing branch. `unknown_target` goes back to meaning exactly what it says | `domain/validity.py`, `domain/patch.py`, tests; `interventions.md` OQ5, `branches-and-worlds.md` OQ3, `validity.md` |
15	| K7 | **Where "no market" gets its reason** | **The tile says `no market` and nothing else.** The reason moves to the Inspector and the chip's hover/accessible name, written once in `spec/vocabulary.md` and chosen by `kind`: a `market` claim — "no venue quotes this claim; what you would trade is on the payoff"; an `event` or `hypothesis` — "no venue quotes this claim"; a `not_tradeable` ending keeps **its own stored reason on the tile**, because that one is a finding | `vocabulary.md`, `tiles-ports-wires.md`, `inspector.md`, `keyboard-and-access.md`; `Tile.tsx`, `fixtureSource.ts` |
16	| K8 | **Zoom** | **Derived, not chosen:** summary tiles below `11/13 ≈ 0.85`; zoom floor `11/22 = 0.5`. Both are consequences of "text never below 11 pixels". No counter-scaling. Supersedes the plan's 0.6 | `layout-and-zoom.md`; `graph/geometry.ts` (already done) |
17	| K9 | **Tile height** | **Content-fit, clamped 152–272 px, on the 8-px grid, computed from the content** (never measured from the screen, so layout stays a pure function). The chapter's "96–216" is corrected | `tiles-ports-wires.md`; `geometry.ts` (already done) |
18	| K10 | **The rail's column heading** | On screen the column reads **"same direction"**. The field stays `agreement`. The word *agreement* on screen is left free for stack 04's run-to-run number. The other column reads **"how firm"** | `vocabulary.md`, `diff-view.md`, `diff.md` (one line) |
19	| K11 | **Chip layout** | **Stacked, as built:** owner, the number, the range beneath. The one-line form `.61 (.45–.74)` stays for prose, the outline and the accessible name | `tiles-ports-wires.md`, `keyboard-and-access.md` |
20	
21	## The fourteen small ones — approved as a block ("Yes, take all 14")
22	
23	| Question | Decision | Why |
24	|---|---|---|
25	| FR-21 / record 0014 say "its own base rate" | Amend both, dated, to "its own **prior**" | B has no base rate; what varies between versions is `prior`. A factual repair |
26	| Union layout slides every base claim one column right | Following focus is enough, plus: **creating a claim moves focus to it**, so `setCenter` frames the strike. Do not pin columns | The shift is a rigid translation; pinning would put a cause to the right of its effect |
27	| `h`/`l` among several wires | Nearest on the cross-axis; the others become the `j`/`k` set where you land. The status line names the wire taken | Two keystrokes reach any neighbour; a chooser overlay is a pop-up in all but name |
28	| Which path the path-product bar shows | The same best-backed path the ranking uses (K5); the bar names its steps | One path-choosing rule, used twice |
29	| "+n more" | First seven in the layout's own within-column order; activating "+n more" opens the **outline view** filtered to that column | Reuses two things that exist and are deterministic |
30	| `apply` and a failing edit | Stop at the first edit that does not fit; report **every** violation that edit produced | Later edits may name things the failed edit would have added |
31	| `observe` carries no date | Leave it; close `interventions.md` OQ3: you can only observe the past, and the window starts today, so `at = None` ⇒ day zero is exactly right | `Do` needs a date because a supposition can be about the future |
32	| An `impulse` with no `half_life` | A new violation code, **`impulse_without_half_life`**, checked by `validate`. Reject, never repair | The mirror of `half_life_without_impulse` (#16): the shape and its parameters must agree, checked both ways |
33	| A `ramp` with `lag = 0.0` | Nothing to decide: evaluate the `u ≥ L` branch first and the rise branch is empty. One sentence says a zero-lag ramp behaves as a step, as a *consequence* | No division by zero, no special case |
34	| Two arrows undermine a supposition on the same day | The arrow whose introducing edit came first in the branch; within one edit, its position in `Insert.links`; base-map arrows by `graph.links` order | Both orderings already exist and are load-bearing; replay holds |

3	Catalyst is the agent layer for finance. We turn natural language — a thesis, strategy, hedge, or trading idea — into live execution across any market, venue, or asset class from prediction markets to commodities to tokens to private markets. 15	| `docs/adr/` | Numbered decision records (MADR format: context, options, decision, consequences); `template.md`; `README.md` index. Higher number supersedes |

19	| `docs/initial-brainstorming.md` | Kent's raw notes; the origin of trigger/sustain links and refinement |
20	| `backend/` | The Python server. `domain/` is the pure core — the rules of the map, no network, no model, no clock — and it is property-tested against maps nobody wrote by hand |

24	
25	* **ADR-gated cadence.** An agent drafts the ADR and spec first; Kent accepts, rejects, or amends; only then is code written. Nothing is implemented against a `proposed` ADR. Decisions Kent has already taken are listed in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §3 — do not re-litigate them.

31	* **Research reports are inputs.** Where a report and an ADR disagree, the ADR wins; where an ADR and the PRD disagree, fix the drift in the same PR.
32

34

38	* Specs should follow best practices regarding spec-driven development. Some key aspects of specs for this repo should include invariants and anti-patterns
39	* This is an experimental prototype and I am a solo developer. However, I would like to use best practices regarding commit messages, PRs, and PR stacks to maintain the navigability, hygiene, and legibility of this repo.

For example, if the Strait of Hormuz opening would lead to a decrease in oil prices, they want to know exactly why and how to audit that. They also want to know what would happen if some of these downstream events were different (say the Strait of Hormuz opened but Iran was struck the next day, how would oil prices change then?)

For this assignment, we want to design and build a tool that creates and visualizes causal chains based off of hypothesized events, specifically for a financial use case. Users should then be able to explore the “multiverse” of events by modifying individual events in the chain and seeing what the downstream effects of that change are.

Some things that people are going to want to do is see how black swan events affect their risks, what events could lead to stop losses/take profits, whether certain hypothesized events will actually lead to the financial effects they want, etc.

___

The format of this deliverable can be whatever you want, but it should both be engaging for users to explore through, as well as easily understandable and actually useful. We want to balance both form and function. The exact design and functionality is up to you! We want to see how you explore and take this basic idea.

The final stage of the tool should help the user create a thesis/strategy that they can trade on.

Remember that users have two main use cases here:

1. Is there a reasonable chain going from Event A to a concluding Event B? (Does the Strait of Hormuz opening logically lead to oil prices decreasing?)

Or

2. Given Event A, what are some Event B, C, Ds I can trade on? (If the Strait of Hormuz opens, what are the downstream events?)
___

The Strait of Hormuz is going to open next week.

Republicans win the House but Democrats take the senate during the Midterm.

1	# PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md — Katalyst
2	
3	> A causal-chain workbench for finance. You state a hypothesis; it builds an auditable graph of downstream events toward tradeable effects; you bend any link and watch the multiverse re-propagate; it ends in a thesis with a stop-loss you can name.
4	
5	**Status:** living document (L1.11: there is no shipping, only current state). **Owner:** Kent Gang. **Reader:** the Catalyst team (see §2). **Derived from:** `ASSIGNMENT.md`, `docs/initial-brainstorming.md`, `docs/research/*`, and the 2026-09-16 interview (§3). **Governed by:** `AGENTS.md`. **Companions:** `ARCHITECTURE.md` (how the system is shaped — the technical counterpart to this document), `docs/adr/` (numbered decision records — a journal), `spec/` (the detailed spec, organized as a book by idea).
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. What this is, in one screen
10	
11	**The hero use case, in one sentence.** You type an event you think will happen. Katalyst shows what it would cause, step by step, ending in trades — and lets you change any step to see how the trades change.
12	
13	**Input.** "The Strait of Hormuz is going to open next week." Optionally, a destination: "does that get me to Brent under $70?" Optionally, how likely *you* think it is — or "I don't know."
14	
15	**Output.** A map of cause and effect. Each box is a claim that can be checked by a date ("Brent closes under $70 by Nov 1, per ICE settlement"). Each box shows how likely it is as three numbers side by side: what the model thinks, what you think, and what the market is pricing. Each arrow states the mechanism, how strongly it pushes, and how long it takes. The map draws itself as the model reasons. It ends in things you can trade: a ticker, a contract, a commodity price.
16	
17	**The move.** Click any box and change it: "…but Iran is struck the next day." The original map is kept. A new version forks off. Only the boxes downstream of your change update. A faded overlay shows exactly what moved. Do this as often as you like and compare versions.
18	
19	**The finale.** A thesis card: what to buy or sell, when to enter, the one event that would prove the idea wrong (that is your stop-loss), the event that means take profit, and the rare disasters listed one by one rather than hidden inside an average. Exportable in a form a trading system can read.
20	
21	**Two doors, one map.** *Explore:* "Hormuz opens — what happens next, and what can I trade?" *Verify:* "Does Hormuz opening actually lead to cheaper oil — and where is that chain weakest?" Same map. Verify adds a destination, so the map grows toward it and grades every step. Explore is the first screen; Verify is one extra field, not a second product.
22	
23	**What it is not.** Not a chatbot with a diagram attached. Not an oracle: it lays out an argument, and every number can show why. Not a swarm of simulated agents. Not a place to execute trades.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## 2. Who reads this, and what "good" means to them
28	
29	Catalyst (`catalyst.app`) is 4–5 engineers from Jane Street / DRW / Citadel / Jump, seed-funded by Sequoia and Jump, already shipping natural-language → backtest → execution with a custom query language. They sit *downstream* of this tool. They will not be impressed by another front door to an LLM; they will be impressed by a tool that turns a vague belief into something with a venue, a strike, an entry, a stop, and a falsifiability test — and does so honestly.
30	
31	The brief names three wants: **(a)** how black-swan events affect risk, **(b)** which events trigger stop-loss / take-profit, **(c)** whether a hypothesized event actually leads to the desired financial effect. Each maps to a first-class surface below: the *Tail strip* (a), *Invalidation derivation* (b), *Verify door + conjunctive honesty bar* (c).
32

57	## 4. Vocabulary
58	
59	Every doc, identifier, and UI label uses these words exactly. Full definitions in `spec/vocabulary.md`.
60	
61	| Term | Meaning |
62	|------|---------|
63	| **Hypothesis** | The user's root input: a proposition asserted as true (the `do` intervention below), carrying the user's own likelihood estimate |
64	| **Proposition** (node) | A *resolvable* claim: criteria, adjudicating source, resolve-by date. Kinds: `hypothesis`, `event`, `market` (instrument-bearing terminal) |
65	| **Link** (edge) | A causal claim from one proposition to another: `mode` (`trigger` — domino, fires once, decays; `sustain` — desk-holds-apple, effect retracts if cause is removed), `strength` (how much it shifts the odds of the next proposition; on a log-odds scale so several links add up), `lag`, `shape` (`impulse` \| `step` \| `ramp`), `half_life`, `rationale`, `sources`, `provenance` |
66	| **Provenance** | Where a number or link came from: `asserted` (model, no evidence) · `argued` (model + mechanism) · `documented` (cited sources) · `market_implied` (live price) · `historical` (event study) · `user` · `simulated` (probe) |
67	| **Belief** | A probability with an honest interval `{p, lo, hi}` and an owner: `model` \| `user` \| `market`. The three are never merged |
68	| **Graph** | Propositions and links with no loops (a directed acyclic graph). Loops are legal only through `reflexive` links — a market feeding back on the world — which must have a delay and unroll over time |
69	| **Intervention** | One of `do` (assert; cut parents; the button reads **Suppose this is true**), `observe` (learn; update parents too; the button reads **This happened**), `insert` (add a proposition + links), `retune` (change a link), `refine` (expand a proposition into sub-propositions that must marginalize back), `believe` (record the user's own belief on a proposition; shown beside the model's, not propagated in v1) |
70	| **Branch** | A named, ordered list of interventions over a base graph. A branch *is* a patch; branches compose by concatenation |
71	| **World** | A base graph with a branch applied and beliefs propagated. The base world is a branch with zero interventions |
72	| **Diff** | The structural and belief delta between two worlds: `unchanged` / `shifted` / `added` / `killed` per node, plus ranked terminal deltas |
73	| **Probe** (stretch) | Extra compute attached to one proposition: thousands of random simulations (Monte Carlo), a small probability model (Bayesian sub-net), or role-played experts hunting for gaps (persona red-team). Output re-enters the graph as a `simulated` belief |
74	| **Thesis** | The compiled trade: legs, entry, invalidation node, take-profit node, distribution, tails, caveats |

78	## 5. The hero flow
79	
80	```
81	 Launchpad ─▶ Hypothesis (+ optional target, + optional prior)
82	     │
83	     ▼
84	 Streaming generation ─▶ Graph grows layer by layer; wires draw in propagation order;
85	     │                   belief chips resolve last. Reasoning arrives as it is produced.
86	     ▼
87	 Inspect ─▶ any node/link: rationale, sources, base rate, model|user|market beliefs,
88	     │      "falsified if", conjunctive product of the path from the hypothesis
89	     ▼
90	 Intervene ─▶ "…but Iran is struck the next day" ⇒ branch forks, downstream re-propagates,
91	     │        ghost overlay + delta rail + one-line diff.  A ⇄ A′ on one key.
92	     ▼
93	 Drill down (stretch) ─▶ attach a probe where the thesis is most sensitive
94	     │
95	     ▼
96	 Thesis ─▶ card + live prices + export.  Invalidation node is derived, not typed.

101	## 6. Functional requirements
102	
103	Priority: **P0** — the hero flow does not exist without it. **P1** — the tool is not credible without it. **P2** — stretch; documented, designed for, not built first.
104	
105	### 6.1 Input and doors
106	- **FR-1 (P0)** Natural-language hypothesis input. Explore door (no target) or Verify door (target proposition B).
107	- **FR-2 (P0)** Ask for the user's own likelihood estimate at input as a range slider with an explicit "I don't know" state. Stored as a `user` belief on the hypothesis; never overwritten by the model.
108	- **FR-3 (P0)** Launchpad empty state seeds the four `ASSIGNMENT.md` examples as one-click cards. No illustration.
109	
110	### 6.2 Generation
111	- **FR-4 (P0)** The engine produces a graph in which every proposition is resolvable (INV-1) and every link carries mechanism, strength, lag, shape, provenance, and ≥1 source or an explicit `asserted` mark (INV-2).
112	- **FR-5 (P0)** Generation streams. Propositions and links arrive one at a time over server-sent events (a one-way stream from server to browser) and render as they arrive; layout reserves space so the graph grows without reflowing violently.
113	- **FR-6 (P0)** Every graph terminates in ≥1 `market` proposition, or in an explicit "not tradeable — because…" terminal (INV-9).
114	- **FR-7 (P0)** Verify door returns a graded path A→B or an explicit `no_path` verdict with the nearest reachable proposition. Never a fabricated bridge.
115	- **FR-8 (P1)** Ensemble: N independent generations reconciled into one graph; run-to-run disagreement surfaces as link *agreement* — a number computed from how far the independent runs differed, never a self-report by the model.
116	- **FR-9 (P1)** Adversarial critique pass before beliefs are final. **(P2)** Persona red-teams ("Lloyd's underwriter", "OPEC desk") that propose *missing* propositions and links — hypothesis diversity, not outcome simulation.
117	
118	### 6.3 Audit
119	- **FR-10 (P0)** Inspector (a panel, never a modal) for any proposition or link: rationale, sources, base rate and reference class, the three beliefs, "falsified if", resolution criteria.
120	- **FR-11 (P0)** Conjunctive honesty bar: for any path from the hypothesis to a selected proposition, show the product of link probabilities beside the narrative headline (INV-8).
121	- **FR-12 (P0)** Provenance is visibly encoded on every link and belief chip (INV-2, UX-6).
122	- **FR-13 (P0)** Replay: any world is reproducible from `(base graph id, branch, seed)`. Generation transcripts are stored with the graph.
123	
124	### 6.4 Multiverse
125	- **FR-14 (P0)** Interventions `do`, `observe`, `insert`, `retune`, `believe` on any proposition; committing one forks a branch implicitly; the base world is immutable (INV-5).
126	- **FR-15 (P0)** Re-propagation is local: only the intervened proposition and its descendants change; `sustain` links retract, `trigger` links do not (INV-4).
127	- **FR-16 (P0)** Diff: ghost overlay of A under A′ in a shared union layout; delta rail of terminal changes ranked by **the size of the move × the weakest backing on the best-backed route** from a differing edit's subject to that terminal — over every such route, the one whose weakest arrow is strongest (amended 2026-09-17; "shortest path" and "which edit" both leave the rule). Range width and **agreement** are shown beside as their own columns, never multiplied in — multiplying width in would sink exactly the claims FR-21 floats. A claim counts as **shifted** when it moved by .005 or more **and** moved in the same direction in at least 90% of versions of the map; that share is the agreement. One-line natural-language diff.
128	- **FR-17 (P1)** Compare ≥3 branches as small multiples; at most 4 branches visible, rest collapsed to a list; branches must be named.
129	- **FR-18 (P1)** `refine`: expand a proposition into sub-propositions; the children's combined likelihood must equal the parent's — they marginalize back (INV-10). This is the brainstorm's "search deeper lines".
130	
131	### 6.5 Sensitivity and drill-down
132	- **FR-19 (P1)** Sensitivity sweep: one-at-a-time flips of every proposition, ranking by adverse Δ on each terminal. Feeds FR-23 and FR-21.
133	- **FR-20 (P2)** Probes: attach a Monte Carlo, a Bayesian sub-net, or a persona red-team to one proposition; results re-enter as `simulated` beliefs with their own provenance and rationale.
134	- **FR-21 (P2)** "Where to spend modeling budget": rank propositions by **each stated range's share of the terminal's band** — how much of the width on the number you care about comes from not being sure of *this* claim — and say so in the UI. On the Hormuz example, 65% of the Brent claim's band is its own `prior`; pin that down and the band goes from 30 points wide to 12. *(Corrected 2026-09-17: read "base rate", and "92% … 29 points wide to 8". The Brent claim has no base rate — the number that varies between versions of the map is its `prior` — and the figures are now the shipped engine's, read on that claim's resolve-by day after the example's window was tuned.)*
135	
136	### 6.6 Risk
137	- **FR-22 (P0)** Tail strip: low-probability / high-magnitude propositions listed in a fixed strip with p, PnL, and a suggested hedge — never averaged into an expected value.
138	- **FR-23 (P0)** Invalidation derivation: the stop-loss is the proposition whose flip most damages the terminal, filtered to those that resolve *before* the terminal and are *publicly observable*. Take-profit is the symmetric case. Sensitive-but-unobservable propositions are listed as *unhedgeable*.
139	- **FR-24 (P1)** Payoff distribution from thousands of random simulations: the 10th / 50th / 90th-percentile outcomes, the average loss in the worst 5% of runs (CVaR₅), the largest peak-to-trough loss, and the chance of being wiped out. The actuarial "wiped out" case gets its own row.
140	
141	### 6.7 Thesis
142	- **FR-25 (P0)** Thesis card: hypothesis, horizon, legs (instrument, direction, size, driving proposition, model p, market p, edge), entry, invalidation, take-profit, distribution (P1), tails, caveats (weakest links, unhedgeable sensitivities, crowding).
143	- **FR-26 (P1)** Live read-only prices: Polymarket first, FRED second, Kalshi third. Shown beside model and user beliefs as the `market` belief. Cross-venue disagreement is surfaced, not averaged. FRED data renders the required attribution line ("This product uses the FRED® API but is not endorsed or certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis").
144	- **FR-27 (P1)** Strategy export: a declarative JSON document (schema in `spec/thesis/`) with legs, conditions, and the graph references that justify each — the shape a downstream trading agent could ingest.
145	
146	### 6.8 Grounding
147	- **FR-28 (P1)** Evidence retrieval at generation time (server-side web search); sources attach to links with direction and weight.
148	- **FR-29 (P2)** Historical-analog panel: for a link, past instances and how prices moved around them, with an uncertainty band (an event study).
149	- **FR-30 (P2)** Pastcast self-test: run a chain on a resolved 2024–25 event with a date-frozen corpus and show the Brier score (the standard accuracy score for probability forecasts; lower is better), including when it is bad.

151	### 6.9 Persistence and sharing
152	- **FR-31 (P0)** Sessions (graph + branches + transcripts) persist to a single SQLite file (a one-file database, no server) and are addressable by URL. No accounts in v1.

156	## 7. UI/UX requirements — the *Workbench*
157	
158	The direction is D3. The research's "Instrument" craft rules (typography, color, motion) still apply; the *shell* is a workbench, not a terminal.
159	
160	- **UX-1 Node tiles are rich.** A proposition renders as a card with: claim, kind silhouette, belief chips (model | user | market) as a three-up, a density sparkline when quantitative, evidence clippings (source favicon + one line), and the resolve-by date. Fixed width, clamped height, 8px grid. Detail lives in the Inspector, not the tile.
161	- **UX-2 Ports and wires are typed.** Propositions have input and output ports; a link is a wire whose *stroke* encodes signal shape (impulse: dot-dash; step: solid; ramp: gradient) and whose *weight* encodes |strength|; `sustain` wires are double-stroked; `reflexive` wires loop with a visible lag chip. The midpoint chip shows the conditional probability in the Metaculus arrow-and-bar idiom.
162	- **UX-3 World state is visible.** A strip shows the terminal instruments as gauges (Brent, a basket, a contract) with their model | user | market readings, re-ticking on intervention. Time is a scrubbable axis; lags are real distances.
163	- **UX-4 Level of detail by zoom.** Far: worlds and their terminal deltas. Mid: wiring and belief chips. Near: the full tile with evidence. Text never shrinks below 11px; the tile changes representation instead.
164	- **UX-5 Organizability.** Users can pin, group, and annotate tiles (mood-board affordance); automatic layered layout (the ELK library, left→right) is the default and re-layout preserves the focused tile's screen position. Dragging is either fully supported or absent — never half.
165	- **UX-6 Color is law.** Probability → luminance/opacity. Direction of financial effect → blue ▲ / amber ▼, always with glyph and sign, never red/green. Branch identity → a small ordered palette on lanes and chips only. Tail risk → hatch texture, not hue. Provenance → stroke style (`asserted` dashed). No information in hue alone (INV-12).
166	- **UX-7 Motion budget.** Three animations: propagation wave (wires draw in causal order, ~200ms staggered), branch creation, belief number-roll. Everything else ≤120ms opacity. `prefers-reduced-motion` keeps ordering and drops tweening.
167	- **UX-8 Streaming is the loading state.** No spinner. Skeleton tiles appear at their layer, claims stream in, wires draw, chips resolve last. Reasoning arrives as it is produced.
168	- **UX-9 Keyboard first.** `⌘K` palette; `j/k` siblings; `h/l` layers along wires; `E` intervene; `B` branch; `Space` A⇄A′; `?` sheet. Focus is always visible.
169	- **UX-10 No modals.** One persistent Inspector; confirmations are undoable toasts.
170	- **UX-11 Typography.** One UI face and one tabular-figures mono for every number; three sizes, three weights; hierarchy by color and spacing. Not the component library's defaults.
171	- **UX-12 Themes and access.** Dark-first, light verified, semantic tokens. All text and glyphs ≥4.5:1. The graph also exists as an outline (`role="tree"`) with a screen-reader announcement (`aria-live`) when a branch re-propagates.
172	- **UX-13 Empty and edge states.** Launchpad (FR-3); `no_path` verdict as a first-class card; "not tradeable — because…" terminal as a first-class card.
173	- **UX-14 An overridden assertion says so.** A claim the user supposed true, and that a later edit in the same branch has pushed back down, never renders as plainly true. Its tile carries both states in order — *Supposed · Oct 1 → Retracted · Oct 2 by "confirmed strike on Iranian territory"* — naming the edit responsible, and the branch panel lists that branch's edits in the order they were made. This is what makes the rule that a later `insert` outranks an earlier assertion readable on screen rather than surprising.

177	## 8. Non-functional requirements
178	
179	- **NFR-1 Honesty.** Beliefs render at two significant figures with their interval (`.35 (.2–.5)`), never `.347`. Every number is one click from rationale, sources, base rate.
180	- **NFR-2 Determinism.** Propagation is pure and seeded; the same `(graph, branch, seed)` yields byte-identical worlds.
181	- **NFR-3 Tests.** The core graph code is property-tested (the Hypothesis library generates thousands of random graphs and shrinks any failure to a minimal example) against the invariants in §9; the model boundary is tested with recorded API responses ("cassettes") committed to the repo; evals run out-of-band on the four assignment examples. CI is green with no API key (INV-13).
182	- **NFR-4 Docker.** `docker compose up` yields a working app; `docker compose watch` gives hot reload for both halves; a production-ish compose builds slim images with healthchecks. No database service in v1.
183	- **NFR-5 Legibility.** Every architectural decision is a numbered decision record; every feature with invariants has a spec; every PR names the invariant it satisfies; conventional commits with `spec:` and `adr:` types.
184	- **NFR-6 Cost visibility.** Each generation records model, tokens, cache hits, and dollars; shown in the Inspector's transcript view.
185	- **NFR-7 Performance.** 60 tiles render and re-layout in <100ms on a laptop; streaming first-paint within 1s of the first token.
186	- **NFR-8 Secrets.** One `.env.example`; keys read once via settings; a secret scanner (`gitleaks`) runs before every commit; recorded API responses are scrubbed of keys.

190	## 9. Invariants
191	
192	Phrased as checkable statements. Each names the spec that owns it; specs name the property test. If an invariant cannot name a test strategy, it is a wish and belongs in §6.
193	
194	| ID | Invariant | Owner |
195	|----|-----------|-------|
196	| INV-1 | **Checkable.** Every proposition has resolution criteria, a named adjudicating source, and a resolve-by date | `spec/graph/` |
197	| INV-2 | **Says why.** Every link has a rationale and a provenance; a link that claims evidence (documented, historical, or market-implied) carries at least one source. Every belief has an owner | `spec/graph/` |
198	| INV-3 | **Assert is not observe.** Asserting a proposition (`do`) changes nothing upstream of it; observing it (`observe`) may. Two operations, two verbs in the interface | `spec/multiverse/` |
199	| INV-4 | **Locality.** An intervention changes only what is still connected to its subject in the graph the edit leaves behind; every other proposition is byte-identical between the base and the branch. Operational form: the affected-set table in `spec/multiverse/interventions.md`, which names the set for each of the six operations | `spec/multiverse/` |
200	| INV-5 | **Branches are patches.** The base graph is never modified. A branch is an ordered list of interventions. Applying an empty branch changes nothing; applying two branches in sequence equals applying their concatenation. Every world replays exactly from (base, branch, seed) | `spec/multiverse/` |
201	| INV-6 | **No loops.** Ignoring *reflexive* links (a market feeding back on the world), the graph has no cycles; every reflexive link carries a delay greater than zero | `spec/graph/` |
202	| INV-7 | **Honest numbers.** Every belief satisfies 0 ≤ low ≤ p ≤ high ≤ 1 after any sequence of interventions, and is rendered at two significant figures with its range | `spec/graph/`, `spec/workbench/` |
203	| INV-8 | **Chains multiply.** Any displayed path shows the product of its link probabilities beside the narrative headline | `spec/workbench/` |
204	| INV-9 | **Ends in a trade.** Every graph has at least one tradeable terminal, or an explicit "not tradeable — because…" terminal | `spec/graph/` |
205	| INV-10 | **Refinement adds up.** After a proposition is split into finer sub-propositions, their combined likelihood equals the original's within a small tolerance | `spec/multiverse/` |
206	| INV-11 | **Three voices.** Model, user, and market beliefs are stored and rendered separately; no code path averages them | `spec/graph/`, `spec/workbench/` |
207	| INV-12 | **Not by color alone.** Every direction has a glyph, every tail a texture, every provenance a stroke style | `spec/workbench/` |
208	| INV-13 | **Keyless CI.** Continuous integration runs with no model API key; the model boundary is exercised only through recorded responses | `spec/generation/` |
209	| INV-14 | **A stop you can see.** The invalidation proposition resolves before its terminal and is publicly observable; otherwise it is listed as unhedgeable, never used as a stop | `spec/thesis/` |

213	## 10. Anti-patterns
214	
215	Phrased as *do not X, because Y; do Z instead.*
216	
217	1. Do not let the LLM assign IDs or own graph validity — it collides across branches and invents cycles. Mint IDs server-side; validate in the domain layer; reject, don't repair silently.
218	2. Do not re-prompt for the whole graph after an edit — it breaks locality (INV-4) and auditability. Re-propagate mathematically; re-prompt only for `insert` on the affected subtree.
219	3. Do not conflate conditioning with intervention — "P(oil ↓ | Hormuz open)" is correlational. Offer `do` and `observe` as separate verbs and say which one the user is doing.
220	4. Do not average model, user, and market beliefs into one number — the product's value is the gap between them (INV-11).
221	5. Do not render `.347` — precision beyond two significant figures on an elicited number is a lie (NFR-1).
222	6. Do not headline an expected value — tails get their own rows (FR-22). EV hides the wipe-out.
223	7. Do not simulate an agent society to produce outcomes — unvalidated and the audience pattern-matches it as theater. Use personas only to propose missing structure (FR-9).
224	8. Do not use Markov steady states or chaotic dynamics as the engine — these events are one-shot and non-ergodic. Time-unroll lagged links instead.
225	9. Do not ship a force-directed hairball, a spinner-then-dump, a modal, or the component library's default look — each is a D5 veto condition.
226	10. Do not let a chain end in prose — every terminal is an instrument or an explicit "not tradeable" (INV-9).
227	11. Do not type the stop-loss by hand — derive it from sensitivity (FR-23) and show the derivation.
228	12. Do not put a database, auth, or multi-tenancy in v1 — three failure modes and zero value to the reader. SQLite file on a volume.
229	13. Do not implement against a `proposed` decision record (D9).
