"""Minting identifiers, which is why this lives here and not in the rules layer.

Every claim, arrow, map and branch carries an identifier, and our own code makes
all of them — never a language model. A model asked for identifiers reuses them
between calls, collides the moment two branches fork from the same map, and
refers to claims it never created. So the model names a claim by its text and by
where it sits in its own proposal, and this module turns that into a real
identifier.

Why the rules layer cannot do this. Making an identifier that is unique without
any central register needs two things the rules layer refuses to have: the
current time, and a source of randomness. Reading neither is exactly what makes
that layer pure, repeatable and testable against thousands of generated inputs.
So minting happens out here, at the edge, and the finished string is passed in as
an ordinary value.

The rules layer never checks the format of what it is given. That is deliberate,
and it is what lets the stored Hormuz example use identifiers a person can read —
`H`, `C`, `B` — instead of twenty-six characters that teach nobody anything when
a test fails.
"""

from ulid import ULID


def mint_id() -> str:
    """Make one new identifier: unique without coordination, and sorted by creation time.

    The value is a ULID — twenty-six characters, made from the current
    millisecond plus random bits. Two of them made on two machines at the same
    moment will not collide, and sorting a list of them puts it in the order they
    were made, which makes a log of identifiers readable rather than arbitrary.

    Returns:
        The identifier as a plain string, ready to pass into a domain model.
    """
    return str(ULID())

from collections import deque
from typing import Literal

import networkx
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from katalyst.domain.belief import Belief
from katalyst.domain.graph import Graph
from katalyst.domain.ids import PropositionId
from katalyst.domain.proposition import Proposition

ViolationCode = Literal[
    "missing_resolution",
    "missing_rationale",
    "documented_without_source",
    "cycle",
    "reflexive_without_lag",
    "half_life_without_impulse",
    "impulse_without_half_life",
    "belief_out_of_range",
    "no_terminal",
    "no_hypothesis",
    "multiple_hypotheses",
    "dangling_link",
    "market_without_payoff",
    "not_tradeable_without_reason",
    "unknown_target",
    "unknown_link",
    "duplicate_id",
    "edit_not_applicable",
    "worlds_not_comparable",
]
"""The nineteen things that can be wrong: fourteen faults in a map, five refusals.

The first fourteen are what `validate` finds in a map. The last five are what our
own code refuses to do, and no map can carry any of them. Four are about an
*edit*, found when a branch is folded onto a map:

* `unknown_target` — the edit names a claim that is not on this map.
* `unknown_link` — the edit names an arrow that is not on this map.
* `duplicate_id` — an edit adds a claim or an arrow under an identifier that is
  already in use.
* `edit_not_applicable` — this edit cannot be folded onto this map as written.
  Everything it names is there; what it asks for is something this version cannot
  do, or something the shapes allow and the map cannot carry out.

The fifth is about a *comparison*, and it is the one refusal that is not about an
edit at all:

* `worlds_not_comparable` — these two worlds were not built from the same base
  map, the same seed and the same two loop sizes, so subtracting one from the
  other would leave noise rather than the change somebody made.

Stable strings: the browser switches on them, tests assert on them, and they are
never renamed without a migration.
"""

PROVENANCE_CLAIMING_EVIDENCE: tuple[str, ...] = ("documented", "historical", "market_implied")
"""The three ways of saying "a document or a price is behind this number".

An arrow whose provenance is one of these has to cite at least one source. The
other four — `asserted`, `argued`, `user` and `simulated` — claim no outside
evidence, so they are asked for none.
"""

FADING_SHAPE = "impulse"
"""The one shape of push that falls away on its own, and so the one that can have a half-life."""

TERMINAL_KINDS: tuple[str, ...] = ("market", "not_tradeable")
"""The two ways a chain is allowed to end: naming an instrument, or naming why there is none."""

LONGEST_QUOTED_CLAIM = 80
"""How much of a claim a message quotes before trimming it, so the sentence stays readable."""


class Violation(BaseModel):
    """One thing wrong with a map, addressed to two different readers at once.

    `code` and `subject` are for the machine: the interface uses them to highlight
    the tile or wire at fault. `message` is for the person: a plain sentence naming
    the claim by its text. A violation must never be the only record of a
    rejection — the list is stored with the generation transcript so a rejected
    proposal stays auditable.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    code: ViolationCode = Field(
        description="Which rule was broken. One of nineteen stable strings."
    )
    subject: str = Field(
        description=(
            "The identifier of the thing at fault: a proposition id, a link id, the graph's own "
            "id for faults about the map as a whole — including two worlds that cannot be "
            "compared, which names the map they should both have come from — or a branch id "
            "when a chain of branches cannot be put in order. Never shown to the user."
        )
    )
    message: str = Field(
        description=(
            "Interface text. One plain sentence that names the claim or the arrow by its words and "
            "says what is missing. Never contains an identifier."
        )
    )


def validate(graph: Graph) -> list[Violation]:
    """Return everything wrong with this map — all of it, not the first thing found.

    Pure: no clock, no network, no randomness, no logging. Same map in, same list
    out, in the same order, every time. The order is the order of the rules below,
    and within one rule the faults are sorted by the identifier of the thing at
    fault, so the interface can rank them and a test can compare two lists
    directly.

    An empty list means the map satisfies every rule. It does not mean the map is
    *right* — the numbers can still be nonsense. It means the map is well-formed
    enough to be shown to a person and argued with, which is a different and more
    modest claim.

    Args:
        graph: The map to check. It is never changed, and never read for anything
            but the values on it.

    Returns:
        One entry per fault, in rule order, ties broken by subject. Empty when the
        map is well-formed.
    """
    claims = {proposition.id: proposition for proposition in graph.propositions}

# The checks that run on every pull request and on every push to `main`.
#
# Four jobs, named exactly `backend`, `frontend`, `types-fresh` and `docker`.
# The names are not decoration: decision record 0009 makes them the checks that
# must pass before anything reaches `main`, so renaming one here would quietly
# stop it being required.
#
#   backend      the Python half: style, types, tests
#   frontend     the browser half: style, types, tests
#   types-fresh  the browser's types still match the server's data shapes
#   docker       both packaged images still build
#
# No job below is given an API key or any other secret, and no job needs one.
# That is the rule INV-13 in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md`: the whole suite passes
# with nothing configured, because tests replay answers recorded earlier instead
# of calling anything. A test that tries to reach the network fails loudly
# rather than quietly costing money.
#
# Every action used below is pinned to a major version, so a fix arrives without
# a rewrite arriving with it.

name: checks

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# If a second commit is pushed to the same branch while the first is still being
# checked, stop the first. Nobody reads the result of a run that has already been
# replaced.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # The Python half: install exactly what the lock file names, then lint, check
  # types, and run the tests.
  backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: backend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install uv, the tool that installs Python packages
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
        with:
          version: "0.12.15"
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: backend/uv.lock

      - name: Install the exact packages the lock file names
        # `--frozen` means: use the lock file as it is. If it disagrees with
        # `pyproject.toml`, stop, rather than quietly resolving something else.
        # uv reads `backend/.python-version` and fetches Python 3.12 itself.
        run: uv sync --frozen

      - name: Find mistakes
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Check the code is laid out the agreed way
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

      - name: Check types
        run: uv run mypy src

      - name: Run the tests
        # `--record-mode=none` means a test may only replay an exchange that is
        # already recorded. An unrecorded call fails the test instead of dialling
        # out, which is what lets this job run with no key.
        run: uv run pytest --record-mode=none

  # The browser half. `npm run check` is three things in a row: style, types,
  # tests.
  frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Node 24
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install the exact packages the lock file names
        run: npm ci

      - name: Check style, types and tests
        run: npm run check

  # The browser app's types are generated from the server's own description of
  # itself and committed. This job generates them again and fails if the result
  # differs, which is what stops the two halves drifting apart: change a data
  # shape on the server without regenerating, and this goes red instead of the
  # browser breaking later.
  types-fresh:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Node 24
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install uv, the tool that installs Python packages
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6

# The checks that run on every pull request and on every push to `main`.
#
# Four jobs, named exactly `backend`, `frontend`, `types-fresh` and `docker`.
# The names are not decoration: decision record 0009 makes them the checks that
# must pass before anything reaches `main`, so renaming one here would quietly
# stop it being required.
#
#   backend      the Python half: style, types, tests
#   frontend     the browser half: style, types, tests
#   types-fresh  the browser's types still match the server's data shapes
#   docker       both packaged images still build
#
# No job below is given an API key or any other secret, and no job needs one.
# That is the rule INV-13 in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md`: the whole suite passes
# with nothing configured, because tests replay answers recorded earlier instead
# of calling anything. A test that tries to reach the network fails loudly
# rather than quietly costing money.
#
# Every action used below is pinned to a major version, so a fix arrives without
# a rewrite arriving with it.

name: checks

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# If a second commit is pushed to the same branch while the first is still being
# checked, stop the first. Nobody reads the result of a run that has already been
# replaced.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # The Python half: install exactly what the lock file names, then lint, check
  # types, and run the tests.
  backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: backend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install uv, the tool that installs Python packages
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
        with:
          version: "0.12.15"
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: backend/uv.lock

      - name: Install the exact packages the lock file names
        # `--frozen` means: use the lock file as it is. If it disagrees with
        # `pyproject.toml`, stop, rather than quietly resolving something else.
        # uv reads `backend/.python-version` and fetches Python 3.12 itself.
        run: uv sync --frozen

      - name: Find mistakes
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Check the code is laid out the agreed way
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

      - name: Check types
        run: uv run mypy src

      - name: Run the tests
        # `--record-mode=none` means a test may only replay an exchange that is
        # already recorded. An unrecorded call fails the test instead of dialling
        # out, which is what lets this job run with no key.
        run: uv run pytest --record-mode=none

  # The browser half. `npm run check` is three things in a row: style, types,
  # tests.
  frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Node 24
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install the exact packages the lock file names
        run: npm ci

      - name: Check style, types and tests
        run: npm run check

  # The browser app's types are generated from the server's own description of
  # itself and committed. This job generates them again and fails if the result
  # differs, which is what stops the two halves drifting apart: change a data
  # shape on the server without regenerating, and this goes red instead of the
  # browser breaking later.
  types-fresh:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Node 24
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install uv, the tool that installs Python packages
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
        with:
          version: "0.12.15"

          cache-dependency-glob: backend/uv.lock

        working-directory: backend

        run: git diff --exit-code -- frontend/src/api/schema.ts

  # the instructions in `docker/` are still correct, and that is all.

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:

      - name: Set up the image builder

      - name: Build the packaged server image

1	/**
2	 * The seam between the canvas and wherever its numbers come from.
3	 *
4	 * There are two things behind this interface. Today it is the stored example
5	 * route, which serves a map that was written by hand and checked when the
6	 * server started. Later it is the engine, which computes a world from a map, a
7	 * branch and a seed. The canvas is written against neither: it is written
8	 * against the two methods below, so the day the engine lands the only change is
9	 * which object is handed in.
10	 *
11	 * Why a seam at all, rather than calling the route directly: the two halves of
12	 * this product are being built at the same time, by different people, against
13	 * routes that do not all exist yet. A seam is what lets the half that draws be
14	 * finished and looked at before the half that computes is written.
15	 */
16	
17	import type { components } from "../api/schema";
18	import type { WorldRequest, WorldView } from "./types";
19	
20	/**
21	 * One stored example in full: the base map and the branches that go with it.
22	 *
23	 * Taken from the server's own description of itself, because this shape really
24	 * is the server's and re-stating it here would let the two drift apart.
25	 */
26	export type FixtureBundle = components["schemas"]["FixtureBundle"];
27	
28	/** Where the canvas gets a map and a world from. */
29	export interface WorldSource {
30	  /** The base map and its branches, as the stored-example route already serves them. */
31	  readBundle(id: string): Promise<FixtureBundle>;
32	  /**
33	   * One world.
34	   *
35	   * Its numbers are optional: every slot that holds a likelihood may instead
36	   * hold an absence with the reason it is absent. See `types.ts`.
37	   */
38	  readWorld(request: WorldRequest): Promise<WorldView>;
39	}
40

1	/**
2	 * The world source for the engine — **a stub. Nothing uses it yet.**
3	 *
4	 * The routes it names do not exist. They are being written in parallel, and
5	 * this file is here so that the shape of the handover is visible now rather
6	 * than discovered later: when `POST /api/worlds` answers, this class fills in
7	 * and the object handed to the canvas changes in one line of `App.tsx`. No
8	 * component changes, because every component is written against `WorldSource`.
9	 *
10	 * Read this file as a promise about shape, not as working code. Both methods
11	 * throw a sentence saying what is missing. They do not return a placeholder
12	 * world, and they must never start doing so: a world full of numbers nobody
13	 * computed is precisely the thing this product refuses to draw.
14	 *
15	 * The request and reply shapes below are written out by hand rather than taken
16	 * from the server's generated description, because the server has nothing to
17	 * describe yet. When it does, these become the generated types and the hand
18	 * written ones are deleted.
19	 */
20	
21	import type { FixtureBundle, WorldSource } from "./source";
22	import type { WorldRequest, WorldView } from "./types";
23	
24	/**
25	 * What the engine will be asked for: a base map, an ordered list of edits, and
26	 * the seed that makes the answer reproducible.
27	 *
28	 * Not yet sent anywhere.
29	 */
30	export interface WorldCall {
31	  /** Which base map to start from. */
32	  readonly base_id: string;
33	  /** Which branch of edits to apply. Left out, this is the base world. */
34	  readonly branch_id?: string;
35	  /** The seed. The same map, branch and seed must give a byte-identical world. */
36	  readonly seed?: number;
37	}
38	
39	/**
40	 * Calls the engine for a computed world.
41	 *
42	 * **Not wired up.** `App.tsx` hands the canvas a `FixtureWorldSource`; swapping
43	 * in this one is the whole of the change when the routes land.
44	 */
45	export class ApiWorldSource implements WorldSource {
46	  /**
47	   * The base map and its branches.
48	   *

content.content:
### Branch identity

Four hues, used **only** on a branch's lane and its chips and never on a tile's meaning: **violet, teal, rose, slate.** Proposed token names `--branch-violet`, `--branch-teal`, `--branch-rose`, `--branch-slate` (*proposed here* — the hues are settled, the names are not).

**Not amber.** Amber already means "the money moves down", and one hue cannot mean two things. Every branch also carries a **name chip** with its label, so a branch is readable with no colour at all.

### The motion budget

Three animations, and no more.

| # | The move | What it does | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Propagation wave** | Wires draw in causal order, so the eye follows the chain the way the argument runs | about 200 ms each, staggered 60 ms down the map |
| 2 | **Branch creation** | The new lane's colour and name chip arrive, once, with no bounce | about 200 ms *(proposed here)* |
| 3 | **Belief number-roll** | A likelihood that changed rolls from the old figure to the new one | about 200 ms *(proposed here)* |

Everything else is **an opacity change of at most 120 milliseconds** — `--duration-fast`, which already exists. Nothing scales, bounces, springs, loops or idles. Motion here communicates causality and provenance; it is never decoration, and never a way of making a finance tool feel alive.

**Following arrows is reachability, not arithmetic** — no strength is added, no likelihood is
moved, no shape is evaluated. Which claims each operation reaches, and which arrows count, are both
settled in [`../multiverse/interventions.md`](../multiverse/interventions.md): the affected-set
table, and one named rule — *the map the engine works through is the map with feedback arrows set
aside*. Anything asking **what can move** reads that map, these diff states included; anything
asking **what can I walk to** reads the whole map — the hover lens, `h`/`l`, the outline.

On the strike branch: **S** is `added`; **H** is `downstream`, because S → H was inserted *after*
the supposition on H and so is live; **C** and **B** are `downstream` from H and again directly from
S; **N1** through H → N1; **M1** and **M2** from B. And, as a consequence of that rule:

> **R — *OPEC+ announces output restraint* — is `untouched`. Nothing on this branch can reach it.**

R's only incoming arrow is B → R, the **feedback** arrow — a price outcome acting back on what
producers do. Set aside, R has no incoming arrow at all: an ancestor of B, never a descendant of
anything this branch touches. So the screen can say out loud: *your strike moves the oil price, the
insurance premium, both contracts and the diplomatic ending — and it cannot move OPEC's
announcement.* That sentence is the product, and `INV-workbench.41` and `.42` below pin it.

### B3 — The fifth state arrives with the engine, and nothing is deleted

`shifted` — `.61 → .18` with a directional chevron — needs two numbers to compare, so it cannot
exist here. When `ApiWorldSource` is switched on in stack 04 the empty slots fill and `shifted`
appears. **Nothing written in this stack is deleted then, because nothing false was written.** The
authority changes hands: the server's `affected_set` becomes the truth and the browser's structural
states become a **hint that must agree with it**, pinned by a component test on the Hormuz branch. A
browser quietly disagreeing with the engine about what an edit reached is the traceability veto
wearing a disguise.

re-lays-out. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` there is nothing to remove, because there was
never a tween.

The research finding that stated ranges from language models are reliably too narrow is recorded under *More Information* as **input to that decision, not as a decision**.
218:* Good, because it is accurate to .004 on the fixture and has no seed wobble at all.
239:* **Input to a stack 04 decision, not a decision here — stated ranges from language models are reliably too narrow.** FermiEval (2025): a nominal 90 per cent range covered the truth 28 per cent of the time; QuantSightBench (2026) reproduced it; Paleka et al. (*Nature*, 2024) found measured disagreement across runs beats self-report; Halawi (2024) and the AIA Forecaster (2025) both ensemble. The likely shape: a trimmed mean for the point, and the wider of the stated range and the measured spread for the range, the measured number being *agreement*.
240:* **Related records.** ADR-0004 (a `do` is a timed assertion — the warrant for decision A) and its 2026-09-17 amendment; ADR-0005 (amended here in three places, not superseded); ADR-0008 (which owns test names); ADR-0012 (recordings of the system stand in for the system).
=== 0010 outcome ===
## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: "A", because Polymarket and FRED are free or keyless, documented, friendly about rate limits, and between them cover prediction-market contracts and macroeconomic series — the two instrument types the assignment's examples resolve to.

* **Contract.** `GroundingSource` is a `typing.Protocol` — a Python interface any class satisfies by having the right methods — with `search(query) -> list[InstrumentRef]` and `quote(ref) -> MarketBelief` (a probability or level, an interval where the venue gives one, `as_of`, `venue`, `url`). Every adapter caches to disk at `.cache/grounding/<venue>/<key>.json` with a per-venue expiry, so demos and recorded tests stay stable.
* **Polymarket.** A prediction market where contracts pay out on real-world events. Its Gamma interface is Polymarket's public, read-only market-data API: no authentication, read-only `/events` and `/markets`, rate limits of roughly 4,000 requests per 10 s overall, 500 for `/events` and 300 for `/markets` (going over is throttled, not rejected). The geographic restrictions apply to placing orders on the exchange, not to reads. A contract's mid-price — halfway between the best bid and the best offer — becomes `MarketBelief.p` with `provenance=market_implied`.
* **FRED.** The St. Louis Federal Reserve's public economic-data service: a free key passed as a query parameter. Its ALFRED archive stores what each series looked like on a past date, which later lets FR-30's pastcasts show only what was knowable then. The line *"This product uses the FRED® API but is not endorsed or certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis."* is rendered wherever a FRED value appears. The widely repeated 120-requests-per-minute limit is folklore, not documented; the adapter holds itself to 60 per minute.
* **Kalshi (third).** A regulated US prediction-market exchange. Its public market-data reads need no authentication; only account and order endpoints need signed requests. Added only if stack 05 has slack; it is strong on Federal Reserve and inflation markets, so it pairs well with FRED.
* **Semantics.** A `market` belief is *displayed beside* the model's and the user's (INV-11) and feeds the thesis card's `edge` column (model probability minus market probability). Where Polymarket and Kalshi both quote a proposition, both are shown and the spread is called out as a signal, never averaged. A proposition with no quote shows an explicit "no market" state rather than a blank.
* **Rejected.** Metaculus, a forecasting community: every endpoint now requires a token, and community aggregates were removed from general API access on 2026-03-09. `yfinance`, an unofficial wrapper around Yahoo Finance: undocumented scraping, terms-of-service grey area, and aggressive rate-limiting exactly when demoing. Alpha Vantage: about 25 requests a day on the free tier, unusable. Finnhub (60 per minute, documented) is the equities option if a later stack needs tickers.

### Consequences

# The Spec — a book, not a log

Decision records (`docs/adr/`) are a **journal**: numbered because they happen in order. This directory is a **book**: organized by idea, so a reader can open the part they care about and find everything about it in one place. Parts are unnumbered; read them in the order below if you are new.

## Reading order

| Part | The idea in one line |
|------|----------------------|
| [`vocabulary.md`](vocabulary.md) | The words everything else uses, defined once |
| [`graph/`](graph/) | **The language of cause and effect.** Claims that can be checked, arrows that say why, likelihoods that say who thinks so |
| [`multiverse/`](multiverse/) | **Changing one thing.** Interventions, branches, worlds, how a change ripples downstream, and how two worlds are compared |
| [`thesis/`](thesis/) | **From map to trade.** Which step matters most, what would prove you wrong, the rare disasters, and the card you act on |
| [`generation/`](generation/) | **Where the map comes from.** How the model proposes, how proposals are checked, how evidence is attached, how it streams |
| [`workbench/`](workbench/) | **What you see and touch.** Tiles, wires, layout, the diff view, the inspector, color, motion, keyboard |
| [`probes/`](probes/) | **Spending more compute where it counts.** Splitting a claim into finer claims, simulations, role-played experts |

Each part is a directory with a `README.md` landing page (the idea, the terms and invariants it owns, its chapters) and one file per chapter. A chapter is written as the bottom pull request of the stack that implements it, and merges before any code in that stack.

## Shape of a chapter

1. **Purpose** — one paragraph: what a user can do that they could not before.
2. **Data model** — the pydantic models verbatim (pydantic is the Python library that defines and validates our data shapes), plus a diagram where a picture shows a mechanism.
3. **Behaviour** — numbered user-visible flows (`B1`, `B2`, …), each with a worked example on a real event from the assignment.
4. **INVARIANTS** — numbered statements that must always hold, each written as *for all inputs drawn from generator S, statement P holds*, and each naming the automated test that checks it. If no generator can be named, it is a wish, not an invariant, and belongs under Behaviour.
5. **ANTI-PATTERNS** — *do not X, because Y; do Z instead*, each traceable to a real temptation.
6. **Open questions** — dated, so the chapter visibly ages.

Product-level invariants (`INV-1` … `INV-14`) are stated in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §9. A part *owns* the invariants listed on its landing page and refines them into testable form; a part may add local invariants numbered `INV-<part>.<n>`, for example `INV-multiverse.3`.

## Writing rules

Every page stands alone: explain a term where it is used, or link to `vocabulary.md`. No unexplained abbreviations or symbols. Concise and punchy; formatting is a legibility aid, not decoration.

# Stack 04 — generation (04a ∥ 04b)

**Waiting on Kent — five things, and three of them block code.** (1) **Decision record 0015** — where a claim's starting number and its range come from when several independent runs disagree. Kent deferred this to stack 04 on 2026-09-17 (record 0014). It is drafted as `proposed` in 04b's bottom pull request and **nothing in 04b pull request 4 is written until he accepts**. (2) **The repair to `diff.md` open question 7** — an observation almost never puts a row on the change list, because eight worlds per version is too coarse. Two candidate repairs, one recommended, below. (3) **A spending ceiling** for `make record-demo` and `make eval`, both of which call the model for real; nobody runs either until he names a number. (4) **Whether the three non-Hormuz examples get recordings now** — they need his key and his money. (5) For information, not a gate: FR-9's adversarial critique pass is **out** of this stack, with a reason. Ask all five in chat, in that order, on the day this plan is picked up.

---

**Goal:** type any sentence and watch a real map build itself, one claim at a time, with evidence — and with no key, watch the same thing play from a recording. After this stack the four example hypotheses from `ASSIGNMENT.md` all open, the numbers on screen are the engine's, and every proposal the validator refused is visible on the way past.

**What this stack must not do.** No thesis card, no stop-loss, no tail strip, no live market prices (stack 05). No storage — nothing is kept between requests except what a running process holds in memory; the SQLite file is stack 05's (FR-31). No `refine`, no probes, no feedback-arrow unrolling (stack 06). **No re-prompting for a whole map**, ever (anti-pattern 2). **The model never mints an identifier, never declares its own provenance, and never decides whether a map is legal** (anti-pattern 1, record 0003). No graph-to-graph reconciliation across ensemble runs — see record 0015. No pastcast (FR-30, stack 07).

## The shapes sheet — the event vocabulary both stacks build against

Settled here so two stacks cannot answer the same small question twice. **Eight events.** Each is one `event:` name with one JSON `data:` payload, in `backend/src/katalyst/engine/events.py`, mirrored by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`.

```python
class GenerationStarted(BaseModel):     # event: generation_started
    generation_id: str                  # minted by engine/ids.py
    mode: Literal["live", "replay"]
    seed: int                           # what domain/ will propagate with
    hypothesis: str                     # the sentence the user typed
    target: str | None                  # the Verify door's destination, in their words
    recorded_on: date | None            # replay only
    prompt_hash: str                    # which prompt produced this

class ProposalAccepted(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_accepted
    at: int                             # position in the transcript, from 0
    proposition: Proposition | None     # the new claim, identifier minted here
    links: tuple[Link, ...]             # its incoming arrows, identifiers minted here
    frontier: tuple[PropositionId, ...] # claims still open to expand

class ProposalRejected(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_rejected
    at: int
    claim_in_words: str                 # what the model wrote. Never minted, never drawn as a tile
    violations: tuple[Violation, ...]   # domain/validity.py's own codes and sentences

class BeliefsPropagated(BaseModel):     # event: beliefs_propagated
    world: World                        # the whole thing, from domain/propagate

class Verdict(BaseModel):               # event: verdict — Verify door only
    kind: Literal["reached", "no_path"]
    path: tuple[PropositionId, ...]     # empty on no_path
    product: float | None               # the multiplied-out likelihood of that path (INV-8)
    nearest: PropositionId | None       # on no_path: the closest claim the map did reach
    why: str                            # one plain sentence

class Receipt(BaseModel):               # event: receipt  (NFR-6)
    model: str
    calls: int
    input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    cache_read_tokens: int
    dollars: float
    seconds: float
    mode: Literal["live", "replay"]
    recording_date: date | None
    prompt_hash: str

class Done(BaseModel):                  # event: done
    reason: Literal["reached_terminal", "depth_cap", "width_cap",
                    "claim_cap", "model_stopped", "no_terminal", "no_path"]
    claims: int
    links: int
    rejected: int

class Failed(BaseModel):                # event: failed
    message: str                        # one plain sentence. Never a stack trace
```

**The transport is `POST /api/generate` read as a stream, not `EventSource`** (*decided here*). Two reasons, both hard: the request carries a hypothesis, an optional target, an optional user belief and a seed, and `EventSource` can only send a GET with no body; and `EventSource` reconnects by itself, which would silently re-run a generation and spend the money twice. The browser uses `fetch` and reads the body. The wire format is still server-sent events — `event:` and `data:` lines — so the format stays inspectable in a terminal with `curl`.

**A recording is this same stream, line for line** — `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, in order, with a header line carrying the base map, the seed, the date and the prompt hash (record 0012). On replay every event is re-emitted unchanged **except `receipt`**, which is rebuilt with `mode: "replay"`, zero dollars, and the recording's date and hash. Record 0012 names only four event types; the chapter must say all eight and say this.

**Record 0015 — where a claim's starting number and its range come from.** Status `proposed`. Kent deferred it on 2026-09-17 (record 0014). Context: a model's own stated ranges are reliably too narrow — one benchmark measured a nominal 90% range covering 28% of outcomes — and measured disagreement across independent runs beats self-report. **The recommendation to put to him:**

- **Do not reconcile whole graphs.** FR-8 says "N independent generations reconciled into one graph", and matching claims across runs is a similarity judgement with no ground truth — a second, unauditable engine. Instead: build the map **once**, then ask the model **N independent times for each claim's own starting number**, a small cheap call with the same cached prefix. That is affordable, it is exactly the number record 0014 asked for, and nothing has to be matched.
- **The point is the trimmed mean** of the N answers. **The range is `σ = max(stated, measured across-run spread)`** — a measured number with the model's own claim as a floor, never below it.
- **N is 3 for a live run and 8 when recording a demo**, both arguments with those defaults, both measured and put in `STATUS.md`. This answers the standing open question in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §13 and `ARCHITECTURE.md` §10.
- That measured spread is the **second** meaning of *agreement* — how far independent runs differed. `spec/vocabulary.md` already reserves the word and already says: wherever both could be meant, say which. On screen this one is headed **runs agree**; the diff's column stays **same direction** (Kent's K10).
- **Nothing is calibrated and the chip says so.** Record 0014's label is unchanged.

**The amendment to record 0014 — `diff.md` open question 7.** Measured by the engine: learning that B happened moves M1 by `+.063` and M2 by `+.107`, and both come out at **89% agreement**, a hair under the 90% bar, so both read `unchanged`, the rail is empty, and **This happened** looks like a button that does nothing. The cause is that under an `observe` the dice do *not* cancel out of the paired difference: which of a version's eight worlds survive is itself a coin flip. Two candidate repairs:

| Repair | What it costs | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| **Run more worlds under each version while an observation is in force** *(recommended)* | The inner loop only, and only for observed worlds. Eight times the worlds is roughly eight times the inner cost — about half a second on Hormuz at today's 70 ms | **Nothing.** The settled rule stands word for word; one default becomes conditional |
| Read the direction off each version's survival-weighted estimate rather than its raw worlds | Free | Changes what "this version moved this way" means, in a way that has to be explained twice — once in `propagation.md` and once on screen |

**What measuring it involves:** re-run `Observe(target="B", value=True)` on the Hormuz map at `worlds` ∈ {8, 16, 32, 64, 128}, record M1's and M2's agreement and the wall clock at each, and take the smallest that clears 90% with margin. One afternoon, no new code beyond a parameter. ## 04b pull request 2 — the pipeline

```python
# engine/proposal.py — what the model is allowed to return. One of three.
class ClaimProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["claim"]
    claim: str                       # the sentence, as a person would say it
    claim_kind: Literal["event", "market", "not_tradeable"]
    resolution: Resolution           # criteria, judge, resolve-by (INV-1)
    prior: Ranged                    # p, lo, hi. No owner field: we stamp "model"
    base_rate: BaseRate | None
    payoff: ContractPayoff | PricePayoff | None   # required when claim_kind == "market"
    not_tradeable_reason: str | None              # required when claim_kind == "not_tradeable"
    cause: str                       # the identifier of a claim ALREADY on the map
    link: LinkDraft                  # the arrow from that cause into this new claim

class LinkProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["link"]
    source: str                      # both ends already on the map
    target: str
    link: LinkDraft

class Stop(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["stop"]
    why: str                         # one sentence, shown in the transcript

class LinkDraft(BaseModel):
    mode: Literal["trigger", "sustain"]
    strength: float
    lag: int
    shape: Literal["impulse", "step", "ramp"]
    half_life: int | None
    rationale: str
    sources: tuple[SourceDraft, ...] # NO provenance field, and no identifier field

Proposal = Annotated[ClaimProposal | LinkProposal | Stop, Field(discriminator="kind")]
```

**Three things the model is structurally unable to do**, because the fields do not exist: mint an identifier, declare its own provenance, and return more than one thing. A new claim's identifier is minted by `engine/ids.py`; an existing claim is named by an identifier the prompt handed it; `owner="model"` is stamped by us; and **provenance is decided by us from what actually happened** — sources returned by the search tool and cited → `documented`; a rationale with no sources → `argued`; neither → `asserted`. `historical` and `market_implied` come from stack 05's adapters and never from a proposal.

```python
# engine/expand.py
def expand(graph: Graph, frontier: PropositionId, *, target: str | None) -> Outcome
```

One call, one proposal, then `domain.validate` on the map the proposal would leave behind. Accepted → mint, emit `proposal_accepted`. Rejected → emit `proposal_rejected` with **every** violation, and never repair. Both are events; both go in the transcript.

**The caps, all arguments with these defaults** (*decided here*): depth 5 layers · width 3 children per claim · 30 claims in total · 3 refusals in a row on one frontier claim closes that claim · 3 frontier claims expanded concurrently. Record 0006 measures a 30-claim map at about 40 calls.

**Two stop rules that are not caps.** A generation ends at `reached_terminal` when every open frontier claim has closed and the map has at least one `market` or `not_tradeable` ending (INV-9). If the caps are hit with no ending at all, the engine makes **one last call per open claim asking only for an ending** — and if that still fails, the stream ends `no_terminal` and the browser says so honestly. The engine never writes a claim the model did not propose.

**The Verify door.** The destination is added to the map up front as an ordinary claim; every call is told what it is; expansion is steered toward it. `no_path` is returned when the caps are hit and no path from the hypothesis reaches it, naming the nearest claim that was reached. **A bridge is never invented** — there is no code path that adds an arrow to make a path exist, and the eval case whose destination is unreachable proves it.

**Cost.** `engine/receipt.py` folds every call's usage into one `Receipt`. `engine/pricing.py` holds the price table and **nothing else**, with the day it was read and the `claude-api` skill named in a comment. A run whose cache reads stay at zero is a bug, not a slow day.

**Tests** — `backend/tests/boundary/test_expand_cassettes.py`, recordings in `backend/tests/cassettes/`, `@pytest.mark.vcr`, the suite already runs `--record-mode=none` so an unrecorded call fails rather than dialling out:
`test_expand_returns_one_proposal_per_call` · `test_expand_rejects_cycle` (record 0006 and 0008 both name it: a recorded proposal that would close a loop) · `test_expand_rejects_a_claim_with_no_resolution_criteria` · `test_expand_rejects_a_documented_arrow_that_cites_nothing` · `test_expand_surfaces_a_refusal_as_a_rejected_proposal` · `test_expand_reports_a_malformed_answer_and_does_not_crash` · `test_the_model_never_names_an_identifier` · `test_provenance_is_written_from_what_was_found` · `test_a_generation_that_reaches_no_ending_says_so` · `test_verify_returns_no_path_rather_than_a_bridge` · `test_generation_receipt_records_cache_reads` · `test_no_cassette_contains_a_key` · `test_the_pipeline_never_reprompts_for_a_whole_map` (reads our own source, as `test_beliefs_never_merged` does).

**Routes**, in `backend/src/katalyst/api/generate.py`, under `/api/` like everything else:

| Route | Body | Answer |

| `POST /api/generate` | `{hypothesis, target?, user_belief?, seed, versions?, worlds?}` | `text/event-stream` — the eight events, in order, ending in `done` or `failed` |
| `POST /api/generate/insert` | `{base_id, branch, claim_in_words, at}` | One `Insert` intervention — a claim and its arrows, drafted and validated — for the browser to append to its branch |
| `GET /api/generate/{generation_id}/transcript` | — | The transcript of a generation this process still holds |

**`insert` is the one intervention that calls the model** (anti-pattern 2's single exception: re-prompt only for `insert`, and only over the affected subtree). The other five stay pure arithmetic in `domain/`, so a reviewer with no key still gets the whole multiverse at full fidelity.

**Where a transcript lives before stack 05's SQLite** (*decided here*): in memory, keyed by generation identifier, for the life of the process, and streamed to the browser as it is produced. Nothing is written to disk except by `make record-demo`. Writing a second on-disk store now would be a store we have to migrate in stack 05 for no gain today.

**`sse-starlette` is the one new runtime dependency besides the model client** (*decided here*) — a two-file package that gets the framing, the heartbeat and the client-disconnect handling right, all of which are easy to get subtly wrong by hand. If the executor finds it unmaintained, a plain `StreamingResponse` generator is the fallback and the pull request body says which was used.

**Replay** (record 0012), in `engine/replay.py`: no key → the four examples play from `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl` through this same route, at a fixed cosmetic delay that an `instant` flag drops for tests. Beliefs are **not** replayed as numbers: the recording carries the seed and `domain/` re-propagates, so replay and live agree by construction (INV-5). Every recording carries **at least one `proposal_rejected`** and **one recorded intervention** — the scripted "…but Iran is struck the next day" its card offers. Any other insert is declined in plain words: *"drafting a new claim needs a model key."*

`make record-demo` is the only way a recording is written, and a recording is remade whenever a prompt changes — the same checklist line the cassettes already carry. ```python

PROVENANCE_SPREAD: Mapping[str, float] = {
    "documented": 0.15, "historical": 0.15, "market_implied": 0.15,
    "argued": 0.40, "user": 0.40,
    "simulated": 0.50,
    "asserted": 0.60,

Each of the 2 000 versions draws every arrow's strength from a normal centred on the stated strength with that standard deviation, **on the same log-odds scale the strength is written in**. ## The shapes sheet — the event vocabulary both stacks build against

Settled here so two stacks cannot answer the same small question twice. **Eight events.** Each is one `event:` name with one JSON `data:` payload, in `backend/src/katalyst/engine/events.py`, mirrored by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`.

```python
class GenerationStarted(BaseModel):     # event: generation_started
    generation_id: str                  # minted by engine/ids.py
    mode: Literal["live", "replay"]
    seed: int                           # what domain/ will propagate with
    hypothesis: str                     # the sentence the user typed
    target: str | None                  # the Verify door's destination, in their words
    recorded_on: date | None            # replay only
    prompt_hash: str                    # which prompt produced this

class ProposalAccepted(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_accepted
    at: int                             # position in the transcript, from 0
    proposition: Proposition | None     # the new claim, identifier minted here
    links: tuple[Link, ...]             # its incoming arrows, identifiers minted here
    frontier: tuple[PropositionId, ...] # claims still open to expand

class ProposalRejected(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_rejected
    at: int
    claim_in_words: str                 # what the model wrote. Never minted, never drawn as a tile
    violations: tuple[Violation, ...]   # domain/validity.py's own codes and sentences

class BeliefsPropagated(BaseModel):     # event: beliefs_propagated
    world: World                        # the whole thing, from domain/propagate

class Verdict(BaseModel):               # event: verdict — Verify door only
    kind: Literal["reached", "no_path"]
    path: tuple[PropositionId, ...]     # empty on no_path
    product: float | None               # the multiplied-out likelihood of that path (INV-8)
    nearest: PropositionId | None       # on no_path: the closest claim the map did reach
    why: str                            # one plain sentence

class Receipt(BaseModel):               # event: receipt  (NFR-6)
    model: str
    calls: int
    input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    cache_read_tokens: int
    dollars: float
    seconds: float
    mode: Literal["live", "replay"]
    recording_date: date | None
    prompt_hash: str

class Done(BaseModel):                  # event: done
    reason: Literal["reached_terminal", "depth_cap", "width_cap",
                    "claim_cap", "model_stopped", "no_terminal", "no_path"]
    claims: int
    links: int
    rejected: int

class Failed(BaseModel):                # event: failed
    message: str                        # one plain sentence. Never a stack trace
```

**The transport is `POST /api/generate` read as a stream, not `EventSource`** (*decided here*). Two reasons, both hard: the request carries a hypothesis, an optional target, an optional user belief and a seed, and `EventSource` can only send a GET with no body; and `EventSource` reconnects by itself, which would silently re-run a generation and spend the money twice. The browser uses `fetch` and reads the body. The wire format is still server-sent events — `event:` and `data:` lines — so the format stays inspectable in a terminal with `curl`.

**A recording is this same stream, line for line** — `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, in order, with a header line carrying the base map, the seed, the date and the prompt hash (record 0012). On replay every event is re-emitted unchanged **except `receipt`**, which is rebuilt with `mode: "replay"`, zero dollars, and the recording's date and hash. Record 0012 names only four event types; the chapter must say all eight and say this.

| `evaluation.md` | The cassette layer; the four eval cases and their structural assertions; the scorecard; what is deliberately not measured (wording, narrative quality) |

**Record 0015 — where a claim's starting number and its range come from.** Status `proposed`. Kent deferred it on 2026-09-17 (record 0014). Context: a model's own stated ranges are reliably too narrow — one benchmark measured a nominal 90% range covering 28% of outcomes — and measured disagreement across independent runs beats self-report. **The recommendation to put to him:**

- **Do not reconcile whole graphs.** FR-8 says "N independent generations reconciled into one graph", and matching claims across runs is a similarity judgement with no ground truth — a second, unauditable engine. Instead: build the map **once**, then ask the model **N independent times for each claim's own starting number**, a small cheap call with the same cached prefix. That is affordable, it is exactly the number record 0014 asked for, and nothing has to be matched.
- **The point is the trimmed mean** of the N answers. **The range is `σ = max(stated, measured across-run spread)`** — a measured number with the model's own claim as a floor, never below it.
- **N is 3 for a live run and 8 when recording a demo**, both arguments with those defaults, both measured and put in `STATUS.md`. This answers the standing open question in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §13 and `ARCHITECTURE.md` §10.
- That measured spread is the **second** meaning of *agreement* — how far independent runs differed. `spec/vocabulary.md` already reserves the word and already says: wherever both could be meant, say which. On screen this one is headed **runs agree**; the diff's column stays **same direction** (Kent's K10).
- **Nothing is calibrated and the chip says so.** Record 0014's label is unchanged.

**The amendment to record 0014 — `diff.md` open question 7.** Measured by the engine: learning that B happened moves M1 by `+.063` and M2 by `+.107`, and both come out at **89% agreement**, a hair under the 90% bar, so both read `unchanged`, the rail is empty, and **This happened** looks like a button that does nothing. The cause is that under an `observe` the dice do *not* cancel out of the paired difference: which of a version's eight worlds survive is itself a coin flip. Two candidate repairs:

| Repair | What it costs | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| **Run more worlds under each version while an observation is in force** *(recommended)* | The inner loop only, and only for observed worlds. Eight times the worlds is roughly eight times the inner cost — about half a second on Hormuz at today's 70 ms | **Nothing.** The settled rule stands word for word; one default becomes conditional |
| Read the direction off each version's survival-weighted estimate rather than its raw worlds | Free | Changes what "this version moved this way" means, in a way that has to be explained twice — once in `propagation.md` and once on screen |

**What measuring it involves:** re-run `Observe(target="B", value=True)` on the Hormuz map at `worlds` ∈ {8, 16, 32, 64, 128}, record M1's and M2's agreement and the wall clock at each, and take the smallest that clears 90% with margin. One afternoon, no new code beyond a parameter. The test is `test_an_observation_puts_a_row_on_the_rail`. **Recommend an amendment to record 0014 dated in place** — the precedent is record 0008, amended rather than superseded because nothing in the decision changed. If Kent prefers a number of its own, it becomes record 0016.

## 04b pull request 2 — the pipeline

```python
# engine/proposal.py — what the model is allowed to return. One of three.
class ClaimProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["claim"]
    claim: str                       # the sentence, as a person would say it
    claim_kind: Literal["event", "market", "not_tradeable"]
    resolution: Resolution           # criteria, judge, resolve-by (INV-1)
    prior: Ranged                    # p, lo, hi. No owner field: we stamp "model"
    base_rate: BaseRate | None
    payoff: ContractPayoff | PricePayoff | None   # required when claim_kind == "market"
    not_tradeable_reason: str | None              # required when claim_kind == "not_tradeable"
    cause: str                       # the identifier of a claim ALREADY on the map
    link: LinkDraft                  # the arrow from that cause into this new claim

class LinkProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["link"]
    source: str                      # both ends already on the map
    target: str
    link: LinkDraft

class Stop(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["stop"]
    why: str                         # one sentence, shown in the transcript

class LinkDraft(BaseModel):
    mode: Literal["trigger", "sustain"]
    strength: float
    lag: int
    shape: Literal["impulse", "step", "ramp"]
    half_life: int | None
    rationale: str
    sources: tuple[SourceDraft, ...] # NO provenance field, and no identifier field

Proposal = Annotated[ClaimProposal | LinkProposal | Stop, Field(discriminator="kind")]
```

**Three things the model is structurally unable to do**, because the fields do not exist: mint an identifier, declare its own provenance, and return more than one thing. A new claim's identifier is minted by `engine/ids.py`; an existing claim is named by an identifier the prompt handed it; `owner="model"` is stamped by us; and **provenance is decided by us from what actually happened** — sources returned by the search tool and cited → `documented`; a rationale with no sources → `argued`; neither → `asserted`. `historical` and `market_implied` come from stack 05's adapters and never from a proposal.

```python
# engine/expand.py
def expand(graph: Graph, frontier: PropositionId, *, target: str | None) -> Outcome
```

One call, one proposal, then `domain.validate` on the map the proposal would leave behind. Accepted → mint, emit `proposal_accepted`. Rejected → emit `proposal_rejected` with **every** violation, and never repair. Both are events; both go in the transcript.

**The caps, all arguments with these defaults** (*decided here*): depth 5 layers · width 3 children per claim · 30 claims in total · 3 refusals in a row on one frontier claim closes that claim · 3 frontier claims expanded concurrently. Record 0006 measures a 30-claim map at about 40 calls.

**Two stop rules that are not caps.** A generation ends at `reached_terminal` when every open frontier claim has closed and the map has at least one `market` or `not_tradeable` ending (INV-9). If the caps are hit with no ending at all, the engine makes **one last call per open claim asking only for an ending** — and if that still fails, the stream ends `no_terminal` and the browser says so honestly. The engine never writes a claim the model did not propose.

**The Verify door.** The destination is added to the map up front as an ordinary claim; every call is told what it is; expansion is steered toward it. `no_path` is returned when the caps are hit and no path from the hypothesis reaches it, naming the nearest claim that was reached. **A bridge is never invented** — there is no code path that adds an arrow to make a path exist, and the eval case whose destination is unreachable proves it.

**Cost.** `engine/receipt.py` folds every call's usage into one `Receipt`. `engine/pricing.py` holds the price table and **nothing else**, with the day it was read and the `claude-api` skill named in a comment. A run whose cache reads stay at zero is a bug, not a slow day.

**Tests** — `backend/tests/boundary/test_expand_cassettes.py`, recordings in `backend/tests/cassettes/`, `@pytest.mark.vcr`, the suite already runs `--record-mode=none` so an unrecorded call fails rather than dialling out:
`test_expand_returns_one_proposal_per_call` · `test_expand_rejects_cycle` (record 0006 and 0008 both name it: a recorded proposal that would close a loop) · `test_expand_rejects_a_claim_with_no_resolution_criteria` · `test_expand_rejects_a_documented_arrow_that_cites_nothing` · `test_expand_surfaces_a_refusal_as_a_rejected_proposal` · `test_expand_reports_a_malformed_answer_and_does_not_crash` · `test_the_model_never_names_an_identifier` · `test_provenance_is_written_from_what_was_found` · `test_a_generation_that_reaches_no_ending_says_so` · `test_verify_returns_no_path_rather_than_a_bridge` · `test_generation_receipt_records_cache_reads` · `test_no_cassette_contains_a_key` · `test_the_pipeline_never_reprompts_for_a_whole_map` (reads our own source, as `test_beliefs_never_merged` does).

## 04b pull request 3 — the stream, the transcript, and replay

**Routes**, in `backend/src/katalyst/api/generate.py`, under `/api/` like everything else:

| Route | Body | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/generate` | `{hypothesis, target?, user_belief?, seed, versions?, worlds?}` | `text/event-stream` — the eight events, in order, ending in `done` or `failed` |
| `POST /api/generate/insert` | `{base_id, branch, claim_in_words, at}` | One `Insert` intervention — a claim and its arrows, drafted and validated — for the browser to append to its branch |
| `GET /api/generate/{generation_id}/transcript` | — | The transcript of a generation this process still holds |

**`insert` is the one intervention that calls the model** (anti-pattern 2's single exception: re-prompt only for `insert`, and only over the affected subtree). The other five stay pure arithmetic in `domain/`, so a reviewer with no key still gets the whole multiverse at full fidelity.

**Where a transcript lives before stack 05's SQLite** (*decided here*): in memory, keyed by generation identifier, for the life of the process, and streamed to the browser as it is produced. Nothing is written to disk except by `make record-demo`. Writing a second on-disk store now would be a store we have to migrate in stack 05 for no gain today.

**`sse-starlette` is the one new runtime dependency besides the model client** (*decided here*) — a two-file package that gets the framing, the heartbeat and the client-disconnect handling right, all of which are easy to get subtly wrong by hand. If the executor finds it unmaintained, a plain `StreamingResponse` generator is the fallback and the pull request body says which was used.

**Replay** (record 0012), in `engine/replay.py`: no key → the four examples play from `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl` through this same route, at a fixed cosmetic delay that an `instant` flag drops for tests. Beliefs are **not** replayed as numbers: the recording carries the seed and `domain/` re-propagates, so replay and live agree by construction (INV-5). Every recording carries **at least one `proposal_rejected`** and **one recorded intervention** — the scripted "…but Iran is struck the next day" its card offers. Any other insert is declined in plain words: *"drafting a new claim needs a model key."*

`make record-demo` is the only way a recording is written, and a recording is remade whenever a prompt changes — the same checklist line the cassettes already carry. A fifth continuous-integration job, **`recordings`**, parses every file, checks each holds a refusal, and checks each prompt hash equals the current prompt's. No key in it.

Not in the build (they cost money and are not deterministic).

**The ensemble** — only after record 0015 is accepted. `engine/ensemble.py`: N independent small calls per claim for its starting number, a trimmed mean for the point, `max(stated, measured)` for the range, and the measured spread carried as this stack's `agreement`. **The provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths** — settled by Kent in record 0014 and deferred to here because every arrow on the Hormuz fixture is hand-written `argued` or `asserted`, so doing it in 03a would have widened everything equally and taught nobody anything. Now generation produces arrows that genuinely differ.

```python
# domain/propagation.py
PROVENANCE_SPREAD: Mapping[str, float] = {
    "documented": 0.15, "historical": 0.15, "market_implied": 0.15,
    "argued": 0.40, "user": 0.40,
    "simulated": 0.50,
    "asserted": 0.60,
}
```

Each of the 2 000 versions draws every arrow's strength from a normal centred on the stated strength with that standard deviation, **on the same log-odds scale the strength is written in**. "How well-backed is this" becomes "how wide is this" with no extra elicitation. **There is no `strength_lo` and no `strength_hi`, now or ever** — the spread is derived, never stored. The draw stream is **per arrow**, derived from the seed and a hash of the arrow's own identifier, exactly as the per-claim streams already are, so adding an arrow cannot shift another arrow's draws and version *k* of two worlds still shares its numbers.

**Then:** `make types`, read the regenerated `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` end to end, add `frontend/src/stream/__tests__/eventsMatchSchema.test-d.ts` pinning 04a's hand-written events against it. Update `ARCHITECTURE.md` §1 (the event stream is real), §2 (the recorded loop-rejection test exists), §3 (all eight steps of a generation), §5 (INV-13's "still planned" column empties; INV-8's browser row), §7 (the boundary and evaluation layers become built; refresh the test counts, which say 137 and are wrong), §8 (`evals/`, `backend/recordings/`), §9 (record 0015), §10. ## The shapes sheet — the event vocabulary both stacks build against

Settled here so two stacks cannot answer the same small question twice. **Eight events.** Each is one `event:` name with one JSON `data:` payload, in `backend/src/katalyst/engine/events.py`, mirrored by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`.

```python
class GenerationStarted(BaseModel):     # event: generation_started
    generation_id: str                  # minted by engine/ids.py
    mode: Literal["live", "replay"]
    seed: int                           # what domain/ will propagate with
    hypothesis: str                     # the sentence the user typed
    target: str | None                  # the Verify door's destination, in their words
    recorded_on: date | None            # replay only
    prompt_hash: str                    # which prompt produced this

class ProposalAccepted(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_accepted
    at: int                             # position in the transcript, from 0
    proposition: Proposition | None     # the new claim, identifier minted here
    links: tuple[Link, ...]             # its incoming arrows, identifiers minted here
    frontier: tuple[PropositionId, ...] # claims still open to expand

class ProposalRejected(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_rejected
    at: int
    claim_in_words: str                 # what the model wrote. Never minted, never drawn as a tile
    violations: tuple[Violation, ...]   # domain/validity.py's own codes and sentences

class BeliefsPropagated(BaseModel):     # event: beliefs_propagated
    world: World                        # the whole thing, from domain/propagate

class Verdict(BaseModel):               # event: verdict — Verify door only
    kind: Literal["reached", "no_path"]
    path: tuple[PropositionId, ...]     # empty on no_path
    product: float | None               # the multiplied-out likelihood of that path (INV-8)
    nearest: PropositionId | None       # on no_path: the closest claim the map did reach
    why: str                            # one plain sentence

class Receipt(BaseModel):               # event: receipt  (NFR-6)
    model: str
    calls: int
    input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    cache_read_tokens: int
    dollars: float
    seconds: float
    mode: Literal["live", "replay"]
    recording_date: date | None
    prompt_hash: str

class Done(BaseModel):                  # event: done
    reason: Literal["reached_terminal", "depth_cap", "width_cap",
                    "claim_cap", "model_stopped", "no_terminal", "no_path"]
    claims: int
    links: int
    rejected: int

class Failed(BaseModel):                # event: failed
    message: str                        # one plain sentence. Never a stack trace
```

**The transport is `POST /api/generate` read as a stream, not `EventSource`** (*decided here*). Two reasons, both hard: the request carries a hypothesis, an optional target, an optional user belief and a seed, and `EventSource` can only send a GET with no body; and `EventSource` reconnects by itself, which would silently re-run a generation and spend the money twice. The browser uses `fetch` and reads the body. The wire format is still server-sent events — `event:` and `data:` lines — so the format stays inspectable in a terminal with `curl`.

**A recording is this same stream, line for line** — `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, in order, with a header line carrying the base map, the seed, the date and the prompt hash (record 0012). On replay every event is re-emitted unchanged **except `receipt`**, which is rebuilt with `mode: "replay"`, zero dollars, and the recording's date and hash. Record 0012 names only four event types; the chapter must say all eight and say this.

**Record 0015 — where a claim's starting number and its range come from.** Status `proposed`. Kent deferred it on 2026-09-17 (record 0014). Context: a model's own stated ranges are reliably too narrow — one benchmark measured a nominal 90% range covering 28% of outcomes — and measured disagreement across independent runs beats self-report. **The recommendation to put to him:**

- **Do not reconcile whole graphs.** FR-8 says "N independent generations reconciled into one graph", and matching claims across runs is a similarity judgement with no ground truth — a second, unauditable engine. Instead: build the map **once**, then ask the model **N independent times for each claim's own starting number**, a small cheap call with the same cached prefix. That is affordable, it is exactly the number record 0014 asked for, and nothing has to be matched.
- **The point is the trimmed mean** of the N answers. **The range is `σ = max(stated, measured across-run spread)`** — a measured number with the model's own claim as a floor, never below it.
- **N is 3 for a live run and 8 when recording a demo**, both arguments with those defaults, both measured and put in `STATUS.md`. This answers the standing open question in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §13 and `ARCHITECTURE.md` §10.
- That measured spread is the **second** meaning of *agreement* — how far independent runs differed. `spec/vocabulary.md` already reserves the word and already says: wherever both could be meant, say which. On screen this one is headed **runs agree**; the diff's column stays **same direction** (Kent's K10).
- **Nothing is calibrated and the chip says so.** Record 0014's label is unchanged.

**The amendment to record 0014 — `diff.md` open question 7.** Measured by the engine: learning that B happened moves M1 by `+.063` and M2 by `+.107`, and both come out at **89% agreement**, a hair under the 90% bar, so both read `unchanged`, the rail is empty, and **This happened** looks like a button that does nothing. The cause is that under an `observe` the dice do *not* cancel out of the paired difference: which of a version's eight worlds survive is itself a coin flip. Two candidate repairs:

| Repair | What it costs | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| **Run more worlds under each version while an observation is in force** *(recommended)* | The inner loop only, and only for observed worlds. Eight times the worlds is roughly eight times the inner cost — about half a second on Hormuz at today's 70 ms | **Nothing.** The settled rule stands word for word; one default becomes conditional |
| Read the direction off each version's survival-weighted estimate rather than its raw worlds | Free | Changes what "this version moved this way" means, in a way that has to be explained twice — once in `propagation.md` and once on screen |

**What measuring it involves:** re-run `Observe(target="B", value=True)` on the Hormuz map at `worlds` ∈ {8, 16, 32, 64, 128}, record M1's and M2's agreement and the wall clock at each, and take the smallest that clears 90% with margin. One afternoon, no new code beyond a parameter. The test is `test_an_observation_puts_a_row_on_the_rail`. **Recommend an amendment to record 0014 dated in place** — the precedent is record 0008, amended rather than superseded because nothing in the decision changed. If Kent prefers a number of its own, it becomes record 0016.

## 04b pull request 2 — the pipeline

```python
# engine/proposal.py — what the model is allowed to return. One of three.
class ClaimProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["claim"]
    claim: str                       # the sentence, as a person would say it
    claim_kind: Literal["event", "market", "not_tradeable"]
    resolution: Resolution           # criteria, judge, resolve-by (INV-1)
    prior: Ranged                    # p, lo, hi. No owner field: we stamp "model"
    base_rate: BaseRate | None
    payoff: ContractPayoff | PricePayoff | None   # required when claim_kind == "market"
    not_tradeable_reason: str | None              # required when claim_kind == "not_tradeable"
    cause: str                       # the identifier of a claim ALREADY on the map
    link: LinkDraft                  # the arrow from that cause into this new claim

class LinkProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["link"]
    source: str                      # both ends already on the map
    target: str
    link: LinkDraft

class Stop(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["stop"]
    why: str                         # one sentence, shown in the transcript

class LinkDraft(BaseModel):
    mode: Literal["trigger", "sustain"]
    strength: float
    lag: int
    shape: Literal["impulse", "step", "ramp"]
    half_life: int | None
    rationale: str
    sources: tuple[SourceDraft, ...] # NO provenance field, and no identifier field

Proposal = Annotated[ClaimProposal | LinkProposal | Stop, Field(discriminator="kind")]
```

**Three things the model is structurally unable to do**, because the fields do not exist: mint an identifier, declare its own provenance, and return more than one thing. A new claim's identifier is minted by `engine/ids.py`; an existing claim is named by an identifier the prompt handed it; `owner="model"` is stamped by us; and **provenance is decided by us from what actually happened** — sources returned by the search tool and cited → `documented`; a rationale with no sources → `argued`; neither → `asserted`. `historical` and `market_implied` come from stack 05's adapters and never from a proposal.

```python
# engine/expand.py
def expand(graph: Graph, frontier: PropositionId, *, target: str | None) -> Outcome
```

One call, one proposal, then `domain.validate` on the map the proposal would leave behind. Accepted → mint, emit `proposal_accepted`. Rejected → emit `proposal_rejected` with **every** violation, and never repair. Both are events; both go in the transcript.

**The caps, all arguments with these defaults** (*decided here*): depth 5 layers · width 3 children per claim · 30 claims in total · 3 refusals in a row on one frontier claim closes that claim · 3 frontier claims expanded concurrently. Record 0006 measures a 30-claim map at about 40 calls.

**Two stop rules that are not caps.** A generation ends at `reached_terminal` when every open frontier claim has closed and the map has at least one `market` or `not_tradeable` ending (INV-9). If the caps are hit with no ending at all, the engine makes **one last call per open claim asking only for an ending** — and if that still fails, the stream ends `no_terminal` and the browser says so honestly. The engine never writes a claim the model did not propose.

**The Verify door.** The destination is added to the map up front as an ordinary claim; every call is told what it is; expansion is steered toward it. `no_path` is returned when the caps are hit and no path from the hypothesis reaches it, naming the nearest claim that was reached. **A bridge is never invented** — there is no code path that adds an arrow to make a path exist, and the eval case whose destination is unreachable proves it.

**Cost.** `engine/receipt.py` folds every call's usage into one `Receipt`. `engine/pricing.py` holds the price table and **nothing else**, with the day it was read and the `claude-api` skill named in a comment. A run whose cache reads stay at zero is a bug, not a slow day.

**Tests** — `backend/tests/boundary/test_expand_cassettes.py`, recordings in `backend/tests/cassettes/`, `@pytest.mark.vcr`, the suite already runs `--record-mode=none` so an unrecorded call fails rather than dialling out:
`test_expand_returns_one_proposal_per_call` · `test_expand_rejects_cycle` (record 0006 and 0008 both name it: a recorded proposal that would close a loop) · `test_expand_rejects_a_claim_with_no_resolution_criteria` · `test_expand_rejects_a_documented_arrow_that_cites_nothing` · `test_expand_surfaces_a_refusal_as_a_rejected_proposal` · `test_expand_reports_a_malformed_answer_and_does_not_crash` · `test_the_model_never_names_an_identifier` · `test_provenance_is_written_from_what_was_found` · `test_a_generation_that_reaches_no_ending_says_so` · `test_verify_returns_no_path_rather_than_a_bridge` · `test_generation_receipt_records_cache_reads` · `test_no_cassette_contains_a_key` · `test_the_pipeline_never_reprompts_for_a_whole_map` (reads our own source, as `test_beliefs_never_merged` does).

**`insert` is the one intervention that calls the model** (anti-pattern 2's single exception: re-prompt only for `insert`, and only over the affected subtree). The other five stay pure arithmetic in `domain/`, so a reviewer with no key still gets the whole multiverse at full fidelity.

**Where a transcript lives before stack 05's SQLite** (*decided here*): in memory, keyed by generation identifier, for the life of the process, and streamed to the browser as it is produced. Nothing is written to disk except by `make record-demo`. Writing a second on-disk store now would be a store we have to migrate in stack 05 for no gain today.

**`sse-starlette` is the one new runtime dependency besides the model client** (*decided here*) — a two-file package that gets the framing, the heartbeat and the client-disconnect handling right, all of which are easy to get subtly wrong by hand. If the executor finds it unmaintained, a plain `StreamingResponse` generator is the fallback and the pull request body says which was used.

**Replay** (record 0012), in `engine/replay.py`: no key → the four examples play from `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl` through this same route, at a fixed cosmetic delay that an `instant` flag drops for tests. Beliefs are **not** replayed as numbers: the recording carries the seed and `domain/` re-propagates, so replay and live agree by construction (INV-5). Every recording carries **at least one `proposal_rejected`** and **one recorded intervention** — the scripted "…but Iran is struck the next day" its card offers. Any other insert is declined in plain words: *"drafting a new claim needs a model key."*

`make record-demo` is the only way a recording is written, and a recording is remade whenever a prompt changes — the same checklist line the cassettes already carry. A fifth continuous-integration job, **`recordings`**, parses every file, checks each holds a refusal, and checks each prompt hash equals the current prompt's. No key in it.
